```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOAD CHARACTERISTICS & DEFINE TARGETING SCENARIOS (WITH 5TH GROUP)
# ==============================================================================
chars <- read_csv("customer_characteristics.csv") |>
  mutate(across(-CUSTOMER_NUMBER, ~ as.logical(.x))) |>
  filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER))

all_custs <- unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
n_target  <- round(0.015 * length(all_custs))   # 1.5% launch target

# Total usage (for Scenario 3) and Peak-window usage (for Scenario 4 / Group 5)
cust_use <- sub_df |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    total_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh),
    peak_kwh  = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pick <- function(ids, n = n_target) {
  if (length(ids) <= n) {
    message("Eligible pool (", length(ids), ") <= target (", n, "): using all of them")
    return(ids)
  }
  sample(ids, n)
}

set.seed(42)

# 0) Baseline comparison: random 1.5%
ids_random <- sample(all_custs, n_target)

# 1) Open to new/green tech: solar, heat pump, or EV
ids_green <- chars |>
  filter(is_solar | heatpump | lvl1EV | lvl2EV) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |> pick()

# 2) High peak / off-peak ratio
ids_ratio <- chars |>
  filter(high_peak_ratio) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |> pick()

# 3) High-use "typical curve": not solar, no EV, peak contributor (ranked by total kWh)
ids_typical <- chars |>
  filter(peak_demand_contributor, !is_solar, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV) |>
  inner_join(cust_use, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER") |>
  slice_max(total_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

# 4) NEW 5TH GROUP — Inflexible (no HP, no EV, no solar) with high peak usage
ids_inflexible <- chars |>
  filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
  inner_join(cust_use, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER") |>
  slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

scenarios <- list(
  "Random 1.5%"                                    = ids_random,
  "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"              = ids_green,
  "High peak/off-peak ratio"                       = ids_ratio,
  "High-use, typical curve"                        = ids_typical,
  "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"   = ids_inflexible
)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. SIMULATION FUNCTION (your dispatch logic, unchanged)
# ==============================================================================
cap_kwh <- 20.16; max_kw <- 7.68; rt_eff <- 0.894
eta <- sqrt(rt_eff); taper_frac <- 0.45

simulate_battery <- function(battery_custs) {
  bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
    filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs) |>
    mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
    complete(nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
             hour_ending = 1:24, fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

  kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = avg_kw_before)
  kw_mat <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  n_prof <- nrow(kw_mat)

  per_wide <- kw_wide |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
    left_join(df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
              by = c("month", "day_type"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = tou_period)
  per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0

  soc <- rep(0, n_prof); out_mat <- kw_mat
  for (pass in 1:2) {
    for (h in 1:24) {
      l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0); p <- per_mat[, h]

      is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
      grid_charge <- ifelse(is_charge,
                            pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta), 0)
      soc <- soc + grid_charge * eta

      is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
        (soc > 0) & (l > 0)
      deliver <- ifelse(is_discharge, pmin(l, max_kw, soc * eta), 0)
      soc <- soc - deliver / eta

      if (pass == 2) out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
    }
  }

  bat_after_long <- bind_cols(kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                              as_tibble(out_mat)) |>
    pivot_longer(as.character(1:24), names_to = "hour_ending", values_to = "avg_kw_after") |>
    mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

  sub_df |>
    left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    mutate(
      has_battery = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs,
      kwh_before  = hourly_kwh,
      kwh_after   = if_else(has_battery, avg_kw_after * n_hours, hourly_kwh),
      cost_before = kwh_before * tou_rate,
      cost_after  = kwh_after  * tou_rate
    )
}

sims <- lapply(scenarios, simulate_battery)

# ==============================================================================

              mwh_after  = sum(kwh_after)  / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>

           n_batteries = length(scenarios[[nm]]),
           mwh_diff = mwh_after - mwh_before,
           pct_change = mwh_diff / mwh_before * 100)
})) |>
  arrange(factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak")), scenario)

  arrange(scenario, season, hour_ending)

# Shaded TOU background blocks & labels
shade_blocks <- baseline_df |>
  group_by(season) |>
  mutate(block_id = cumsum(tou_period != lag(tou_period, default = first(tou_period)))) |>
  group_by(season, block_id, tou_period) |>
  summarise(xmin = min(hour_ending) - 1, xmax = max(hour_ending),
            mid_x = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
            label = if_else((xmax - xmin) >= 2, as.character(first(tou_period)), ""),
            .groups = "drop")

tou_colors <- c("Off-peak" = "#0077C8", "Mid-peak" = "#00853E", "Peak" = "#B57A14")

line_colors <- c("Baseline (no batteries)"                       = "#1B2A4A",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

line_types <- c("solid", "dashed", "dotdash", "twodash")
names(line_types) <- scen_levels

p_all <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = shade_blocks,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tou_period),

            color = "grey30", vjust = 1.5, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +

  scale_color_manual(values = line_colors, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = line_types, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(1.2, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9) |> setNames(scen_levels),
                         name = "Scenario") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
                     labels = c("12am", "4am", "8am", "12pm", "4pm", "8pm", "12am"),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.22))) +
  labs(title = "Fleet Load Shift by Battery Targeting Strategy",
       subtitle = paste0("Enphase IQ Battery 10C (20.16 kWh, 7.68 kW, 89.4% RTE) on ",
                         length(scenarios[[group_names[1]]]),
                         " customers per scenario (1.5% of fleet)"),
       x = "Time of Day", y = "Total Weekday Usage (MWh)") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
         linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),

library(dplyr)

inflex_name <- "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"
if (!inflex_name %in% names(sims)) {
  ids_inflexible <- chars |>
    filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
    inner_join(
      sub_df |>
        group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
        summarise(peak_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
    ) |>
    slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

  scenarios[[inflex_name]] <- ids_inflexible
  sims[[inflex_name]]      <- simulate_battery(ids_inflexible)
}

# Two-step scaling: 5,000 sample -> 35,000 full dataset -> 924,544 NYSEG territory
n_sub_custs        <- length(unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) # 5,000
n_dataset_custs    <- 35000                                   # Full dataset
n_nyseg_custs      <- 924544                                  # NYSEG territory

scale_sub_to_35k   <- n_dataset_custs / n_sub_custs           # 7.0x
scale_35k_to_nyseg <- n_nyseg_custs / n_dataset_custs         # 26.4155x
scale_sub_to_nyseg <- scale_sub_to_35k * scale_35k_to_nyseg   # 184.9088x

scen_order <- c("Random 1.5%",
                "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)")
scen_order <- intersect(scen_order, names(sims))

scen_colors <- c("Random 1.5%"                                   = "#7F7F7F",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

# Scaled fleet capacity across all three tiers (1.5% adoption)
n_bat_sub   <- length(scenarios[[scen_order[1]]])       # 75
n_bat_35k   <- round(n_bat_sub * scale_sub_to_35k)      # 525
n_bat_nyseg <- round(n_bat_sub * scale_sub_to_nyseg)    # 13,868

cap_sub_label <- sprintf(
  "Added Capacity (1.5%%): 5k Sample = %s bats (%.2f MWh / %.2f MW)  |  35k Dataset = %s bats (%.1f MWh / %.1f MW)  |  NYSEG = %s bats (%.1f MWh / %.1f MW)",
  comma(n_bat_sub),   (n_bat_sub   * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_sub   * max_kw) / 1000,
  comma(n_bat_35k),   (n_bat_35k   * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_35k   * max_kw) / 1000,
  comma(n_bat_nyseg), (n_bat_nyseg * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_nyseg * max_kw) / 1000
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. COMPUTE METRICS WITH TWO-STEP SCALING
# ==============================================================================
savings_df <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]]

  hrs_per_cust <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(tot_hrs = sum(n_hours), .groups = "drop") |>
    summarise(mean_hrs = mean(tot_hrs)) |>
    pull(mean_hrs)
  ann_factor <- 8760 / hrs_per_cust

  cust_savings <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(annual_saved = (sum(cost_before) - sum(cost_after)) * ann_factor,
              .groups = "drop")

  sub_total_saved <- sum(cust_savings$annual_saved)

  tibble(
    scenario          = factor(nm, levels = rev(scen_order)),
    per_cust_usd      = mean(cust_savings$annual_saved),
    dataset_35k_k     = (sub_total_saved * scale_sub_to_35k)   / 1e3,
    nyseg_total_m     = (sub_total_saved * scale_sub_to_nyseg) / 1e6
  )
}))

peak_df <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]] |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday", month %in% c(12, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8)) |>
    mutate(season = factor(if_else(month %in% c(12, 1, 2), "Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)"),
                           levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)")))

  season_window <- df_sim |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(target_tou = if_else(any(tou_period == "Peak"), "Peak", "Mid-peak"),
              .groups = "drop")

  df_sim |>
    inner_join(season_window, by = c("season", "tou_period" = "target_tou")) |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(
      n_peak_days            = sum(n_hours) / (n_distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) * n_distinct(hour_ending)),
      # Percentage drops are scale-invariant (identical across 5k, 35k, and 924.5k)
      fleet_peak_pct_drop    = (1 - sum(kwh_after) / sum(kwh_before)) * 100,
      enrolled_peak_pct_drop = (1 - sum(kwh_after[has_battery]) / sum(kwh_before[has_battery])) * 100,
      # Single peak event MWh scaled from 5k -> 35k -> NYSEG
      sub_single_mwh         = ((sum(kwh_before) - sum(kwh_after)) / 1000) / n_peak_days,
      dataset_35k_single_mwh = sub_single_mwh * scale_sub_to_35k,
      nyseg_single_mwh       = sub_single_mwh * scale_sub_to_nyseg,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(scenario = factor(nm, levels = rev(scen_order)))
}))

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 1: WINTER & SUMMER PEAK LOAD REDUCTION (% DROP — SCALE-INVARIANT)

plot1_data <- peak_df |>

        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_peak_pct

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 2: SINGLE PEAK EVENT MWh SAVED (35k DATASET VS. NYSEG SCALE)
# ==============================================================================
plot2_data <- peak_df |>

p_single_peak

# ==============================================================================

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. REALISTIC BATTERY SIMULATION (WITH 20% BACKUP RESERVE FLOOR)
# ==============================================================================
cap_kwh      <- 20.16
max_kw       <- 7.68
rt_eff       <- 0.894
eta          <- sqrt(rt_eff)
taper_frac   <- 0.45
min_soc_frac <- 0.20                    # Never drain below 20% (outage backup reserve)
min_soc_kwh  <- cap_kwh * min_soc_frac  # 4.032 kWh reserve floor (16.13 kWh usable)

simulate_battery <- function(battery_custs) {
  bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
    filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs) |>
    mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
    complete(nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
             hour_ending = 1:24, fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

  kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = avg_kw_before)
  kw_mat <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  n_prof <- nrow(kw_mat)

  per_wide <- kw_wide |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
    left_join(df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
              by = c("month", "day_type"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = tou_period)
  per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0

  # Initialize SOC at the 20% backup reserve floor rather than 0
  soc <- rep(min_soc_kwh, n_prof)
  out_mat <- kw_mat

  for (pass in 1:2) {
    for (h in 1:24) {
      l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0)
      p <- per_mat[, h]

      is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
      grid_charge <- ifelse(is_charge,
                            pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta), 0)
      soc <- soc + grid_charge * eta

      # Only discharge energy above the 20% reserve floor (soc > min_soc_kwh)
      is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
        (soc > min_soc_kwh) & (l > 0)
      deliver <- ifelse(is_discharge, pmin(l, max_kw, (soc - min_soc_kwh) * eta), 0)
      soc <- soc - deliver / eta

      if (pass == 2) out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
    }
  }

  bat_after_long <- bind_cols(kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                              as_tibble(out_mat)) |>
    pivot_longer(as.character(1:24), names_to = "hour_ending", values_to = "avg_kw_after") |>
    mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

  sub_df |>
    left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    mutate(
      has_battery = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs,
      kwh_before  = hourly_kwh,
      kwh_after   = if_else(has_battery, avg_kw_after * n_hours, hourly_kwh),
      cost_before = kwh_before * tou_rate,
      cost_after  = kwh_after  * tou_rate
    )
}

# Ensure all 4 active scenarios are defined and re-simulated with the 20% reserve floor
names(scenarios)[names(scenarios) == "Random 5%"] <- "Random 1.5%"
inflex_name <- "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"

if (!inflex_name %in% names(scenarios)) {
  scenarios[[inflex_name]] <- chars |>
    filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
    inner_join(
      sub_df |>
        group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
        summarise(peak_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
    ) |>
    slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
}

scen_order <- c("Random 1.5%",
                "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)")

scen_colors <- c("Random 1.5%"                                   = "#7F7F7F",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

# Re-run simulations with the 20% SOC floor
sims <- lapply(scenarios[scen_order], simulate_battery)

# Two-step scaling: 5,000 sample -> 35,000 dataset -> 924,544 NYSEG territory
n_sub_custs        <- length(unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) # 5,000
scale_sub_to_35k   <- 35000 / n_sub_custs                     # 7.0x
scale_sub_to_nyseg <- 924544 / n_sub_custs                    # 184.91x

# ==============================================================================
# 2. IDENTIFY THE TOP 100 CRITICAL GRID HOURS OF THE YEAR ("TOP 1%" RULE)
# ==============================================================================
# Rank all (month, day_type, hour_ending) buckets by baseline fleet hourly demand
# and select the exact 100 highest-load hours of the 8,760-hour year.
top100_slots <- sub_df |>
  group_by(month, day_type, hour_ending) |>
  summarise(
    slot_hours    = round(median(n_hours[n_hours > 0], na.rm = TRUE)),
    sub_mw_before = sum(if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) / 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(sub_mw_before)) |>
  mutate(
    cum_hours    = cumsum(slot_hours),
    prev_hours   = lag(cum_hours, default = 0),
    weight_hours = pmax(0L, as.integer(pmin(slot_hours, 100L - prev_hours)))
  ) |>
  filter(weight_hours > 0)

# Evaluate each segment across those Top 100 Critical Hours
top100_hourly <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  sims[[nm]] |>
    inner_join(top100_slots |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, weight_hours),
               by = c("month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    group_by(month, day_type, hour_ending, weight_hours) |>
    summarise(
      sub_mw_before      = sum(if_else(n_hours > 0, kwh_before / n_hours, 0)) / 1000,
      sub_mw_after       = sum(if_else(n_hours > 0, kwh_after  / n_hours, 0)) / 1000,
      sub_mwh_saved_hr   = sub_mw_before - sub_mw_after,
      ds35k_mwh_saved_hr = sub_mwh_saved_hr * scale_sub_to_35k,
      nyseg_mwh_saved_hr = sub_mwh_saved_hr * scale_sub_to_nyseg,
      fleet_pct_drop     = (sub_mwh_saved_hr / sub_mw_before) * 100,
      enrolled_pct_drop  = (1 - sum(kwh_after[has_battery]) / sum(kwh_before[has_battery])) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(sub_mw_before)) |>
    # Expand each calendar bucket into individual ranked hours (1 to 100)
    tidyr::uncount(weight_hours) |>
    mutate(
      critical_hour_rank = row_number(),
      scenario = factor(nm, levels = scen_order)
    )
}))

# Summary Table across the Top 100 Hours
top100_summary <- top100_hourly |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(
    avg_hourly_mwh_35k     = mean(ds35k_mwh_saved_hr),
    avg_hourly_mwh_nyseg   = mean(nyseg_mwh_saved_hr),
    total_100hr_mwh_nyseg  = sum(nyseg_mwh_saved_hr),
    avg_fleet_pct_drop     = mean(fleet_pct_drop),
    avg_enrolled_pct_drop  = mean(enrolled_pct_drop),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(top100_summary)

# ==============================================================================
# GRAPH 1: TOP 100 HOURS AVERAGE MWh SAVED & % REDUCTION (VS. 5%–10% TARGET)
# ==============================================================================
p1_mwh <- ggplot(top100_summary,
                 aes(x = avg_hourly_mwh_nyseg, y = reorder(scenario, avg_hourly_mwh_nyseg),
                     fill = scenario)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f MWh/hr\n(%.1f MWh @ 35k)",
                                avg_hourly_mwh_nyseg, avg_hourly_mwh_35k)),
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", color = "#1B2A4A") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = scen_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35))) +
  labs(title = "Top 100 Critical Hours: Average Peak-Hour Reduction (MWh)",
       subtitle = "NYSEG Territory (13,868 batteries @ 1.5% adoption, 20% backup reserve floor)",
       x = "Average MWh Shaved per Critical Hour (NYSEG Scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12.5) +

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. ENSURE 20% BACKUP RESERVE SIMULATION IS APPLIED TO ALL TARGET GROUPS
# ==============================================================================
cap_kwh      <- 20.16
max_kw       <- 7.68
rt_eff       <- 0.894
eta          <- sqrt(rt_eff)
taper_frac   <- 0.45
min_soc_frac <- 0.20                    # 20% outage backup reserve floor
min_soc_kwh  <- cap_kwh * min_soc_frac  # 4.032 kWh floor (16.13 kWh usable)

simulate_battery <- function(battery_custs) {
  bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
    filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs) |>
    mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
    complete(nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
             hour_ending = 1:24, fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

  kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = avg_kw_before)
  kw_mat <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  n_prof <- nrow(kw_mat)

  per_wide <- kw_wide |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
    left_join(df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
              by = c("month", "day_type"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = tou_period)
  per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0

  soc <- rep(min_soc_kwh, n_prof)
  out_mat <- kw_mat

  for (pass in 1:2) {
    for (h in 1:24) {
      l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0)
      p <- per_mat[, h]

      is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
      grid_charge <- ifelse(is_charge,
                            pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta), 0)
      soc <- soc + grid_charge * eta

      is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
        (soc > min_soc_kwh) & (l > 0)
      deliver <- ifelse(is_discharge, pmin(l, max_kw, (soc - min_soc_kwh) * eta), 0)
      soc <- soc - deliver / eta

      if (pass == 2) out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
    }
  }

  bat_after_long <- bind_cols(kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                              as_tibble(out_mat)) |>
    pivot_longer(as.character(1:24), names_to = "hour_ending", values_to = "avg_kw_after") |>
    mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

  sub_df |>
    left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    mutate(
      has_battery = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs,
      kwh_before  = hourly_kwh,
      kwh_after   = if_else(has_battery, avg_kw_after * n_hours, hourly_kwh),
      cost_before = kwh_before * tou_rate,
      cost_after  = kwh_after  * tou_rate
    )
}

inflex_name <- "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"
if (!inflex_name %in% names(scenarios)) {
  scenarios[[inflex_name]] <- chars |>
    filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
    inner_join(
      sub_df |>
        group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
        summarise(peak_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
    ) |>
    slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
}

group_names <- c("Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)")

# Re-run simulations for the 3 plotted groups with the 20% reserve floor
sims_20pct <- lapply(scenarios[group_names], simulate_battery)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. SINGLE OVERLAY PLOT: 4 SEASONS, BASELINE + 3 TARGETING GROUPS (20% RESERVE)
# ==============================================================================
add_season <- function(df) {
  df |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday") |>
    mutate(
      season = factor(case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)",
        month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring (Mar–May)",
        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)"),
        levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Spring (Mar–May)",
                   "Summer (Jun–Aug)", "Fall (Sep–Nov)")),
      tou_period = factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak"))
    )
}

baseline_df <- add_season(sims_20pct[[group_names[1]]]) |>
  group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
  summarise(total_mwh = sum(kwh_before) / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(scenario = "Baseline (no batteries)")

after_df <- bind_rows(lapply(group_names, function(nm) {
  add_season(sims_20pct[[nm]]) |>
    group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
    summarise(total_mwh = sum(kwh_after) / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(scenario = nm)
}))

scen_levels <- c("Baseline (no batteries)", group_names)
lines_df <- bind_rows(baseline_df, after_df) |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scen_levels)) |>
  arrange(scenario, season, hour_ending)

shade_blocks <- baseline_df |>
  group_by(season) |>
  mutate(block_id = cumsum(tou_period != lag(tou_period, default = first(tou_period)))) |>
  group_by(season, block_id, tou_period) |>
  summarise(xmin = min(hour_ending) - 1, xmax = max(hour_ending),
            mid_x = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
            label = if_else((xmax - xmin) >= 2, as.character(first(tou_period)), ""),
            .groups = "drop")

tou_colors <- c("Off-peak" = "#0077C8", "Mid-peak" = "#00853E", "Peak" = "#B57A14")

line_colors <- c("Baseline (no batteries)"                       = "#1B2A4A",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

line_types <- c("solid", "dashed", "dotdash", "twodash")
names(line_types) <- scen_levels

p_all <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = shade_blocks,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tou_period),
            alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_text(data = shade_blocks,
            aes(x = mid_x, y = Inf, label = label),
            color = "grey30", vjust = 1.5, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_line(data = lines_df,
            aes(x = hour_ending - 0.5, y = total_mwh,
                color = scenario, linetype = scenario, linewidth = scenario)) +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tou_colors, name = "TOU Window") +
  scale_color_manual(values = line_colors, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = line_types, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(1.2, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9) |> setNames(scen_levels),
                         name = "Scenario") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
                     labels = c("12am", "4am", "8am", "12pm", "4pm", "8pm", "12am"),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.22))) +
  labs(title = "Fleet Load Shift by Battery Targeting Strategy",
       subtitle = paste0("Enphase IQ Battery 10C (20.16 kWh, 7.68 kW, 89.4% RTE, 20% backup reserve) on ",
                         length(scenarios[[group_names[1]]]),
                         " customers per scenario (1.5% of fleet)"),
       x = "Time of Day", y = "Total Weekday Usage (MWh)") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
         linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
         linewidth = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.1, "lines"))

p_all

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 0. ENSURE ALL 4 SCENARIOS ARE SIMULATED & DEFINE TWO-STEP SCALING
# ==============================================================================
inflex_name <- "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"
if (!inflex_name %in% names(sims)) {
  ids_inflexible <- chars |>
    filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
    inner_join(
      sub_df |>
        group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
        summarise(peak_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
    ) |>
    slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

  scenarios[[inflex_name]] <- ids_inflexible
  sims[[inflex_name]]      <- simulate_battery(ids_inflexible)
}

# Two-step scaling: 5,000 sample -> 35,000 full dataset -> 924,544 NYSEG territory
n_sub_custs        <- length(unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) # 5,000
n_dataset_custs    <- 35000                                   # Full dataset
n_nyseg_custs      <- 924544                                  # NYSEG territory

scale_sub_to_35k   <- n_dataset_custs / n_sub_custs           # 7.0x
scale_35k_to_nyseg <- n_nyseg_custs / n_dataset_custs         # 26.4155x
scale_sub_to_nyseg <- scale_sub_to_35k * scale_35k_to_nyseg   # 184.9088x

scen_order <- c("Random 1.5%",
                "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)")
scen_order <- intersect(scen_order, names(sims))

scen_colors <- c("Random 1.5%"                                   = "#7F7F7F",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

# Scaled fleet capacity across all three tiers (1.5% adoption)
n_bat_sub   <- length(scenarios[[scen_order[1]]])       # 75
n_bat_35k   <- round(n_bat_sub * scale_sub_to_35k)      # 525
n_bat_nyseg <- round(n_bat_sub * scale_sub_to_nyseg)    # 13,868

cap_sub_label <- sprintf(
  "Added Capacity (1.5%%): 5k Sample = %s bats (%.2f MWh / %.2f MW)  |  35k Dataset = %s bats (%.1f MWh / %.1f MW)  |  NYSEG = %s bats (%.1f MWh / %.1f MW)",
  comma(n_bat_sub),   (n_bat_sub   * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_sub   * max_kw) / 1000,
  comma(n_bat_35k),   (n_bat_35k   * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_35k   * max_kw) / 1000,
  comma(n_bat_nyseg), (n_bat_nyseg * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_nyseg * max_kw) / 1000
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. COMPUTE METRICS WITH TWO-STEP SCALING
# ==============================================================================
savings_df <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]]

  hrs_per_cust <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(tot_hrs = sum(n_hours), .groups = "drop") |>
    summarise(mean_hrs = mean(tot_hrs)) |>
    pull(mean_hrs)
  ann_factor <- 8760 / hrs_per_cust

  cust_savings <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(annual_saved = (sum(cost_before) - sum(cost_after)) * ann_factor,
              .groups = "drop")

  sub_total_saved <- sum(cust_savings$annual_saved)

  tibble(
    scenario          = factor(nm, levels = rev(scen_order)),
    per_cust_usd      = mean(cust_savings$annual_saved),
    dataset_35k_k     = (sub_total_saved * scale_sub_to_35k)   / 1e3,
    nyseg_total_m     = (sub_total_saved * scale_sub_to_nyseg) / 1e6
  )
}))

peak_df <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]] |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday", month %in% c(12, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8)) |>
    mutate(season = factor(if_else(month %in% c(12, 1, 2), "Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)"),
                           levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)")))

  season_window <- df_sim |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(target_tou = if_else(any(tou_period == "Peak"), "Peak", "Mid-peak"),
              .groups = "drop")

  df_sim |>
    inner_join(season_window, by = c("season", "tou_period" = "target_tou")) |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(
      n_peak_days            = sum(n_hours) / (n_distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) * n_distinct(hour_ending)),
      # Percentage drops are scale-invariant (identical across 5k, 35k, and 924.5k)
      fleet_peak_pct_drop    = (1 - sum(kwh_after) / sum(kwh_before)) * 100,
      enrolled_peak_pct_drop = (1 - sum(kwh_after[has_battery]) / sum(kwh_before[has_battery])) * 100,
      # Single peak event MWh scaled from 5k -> 35k -> NYSEG
      sub_single_mwh         = ((sum(kwh_before) - sum(kwh_after)) / 1000) / n_peak_days,
      dataset_35k_single_mwh = sub_single_mwh * scale_sub_to_35k,
      nyseg_single_mwh       = sub_single_mwh * scale_sub_to_nyseg,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(scenario = factor(nm, levels = rev(scen_order)))
}))

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 1: WINTER & SUMMER PEAK LOAD REDUCTION (% DROP — SCALE-INVARIANT)
# ==============================================================================
plot1_data <- peak_df |>
  select(scenario, season,
         `Enrolled Cohort Peak Drop (%)`    = enrolled_peak_pct_drop,
         `Total Grid / Fleet Peak Drop (%)` = fleet_peak_pct_drop) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(`Enrolled Cohort Peak Drop (%)`, `Total Grid / Fleet Peak Drop (%)`),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "pct_drop")

  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.72), width = 0.65) +

                               "Summer (Jun–Aug)" = "#E67E22"),
                    name = "Season") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),

  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_peak_pct

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 2: SINGLE PEAK EVENT MWh SAVED (35k DATASET VS. NYSEG SCALE)
# ==============================================================================
plot2_data <- peak_df |>
  select(scenario, season,
         `Full Dataset (35,000 Customers)`     = dataset_35k_single_mwh,
         `NYSEG Territory (924,544 Customers)` = nyseg_single_mwh) |>

                        `NYSEG Territory (924,544 Customers)`),

                                        "NYSEG Territory (924,544 Customers)")))

p_single_peak <- ggplot(plot2_data, aes(x = mwh_saved, y = scenario, fill = season)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.72), width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f MWh", mwh_saved)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.72),
            hjust = -0.12, size = 3.4, fontface = "bold", color = "#1B2A4A") +
  facet_wrap(~ scale_tier, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)" = "#2B5C8F",
                               "Summer (Jun–Aug)" = "#E67E22"),
                    name = "Season") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(title = "Energy Shaved During a Single Weekday Peak Event",
       subtitle = cap_sub_label,
       x = "Single Peak Event Reduction (MWh)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_single_peak

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 3: ANNUAL TOU COST SAVINGS (PER CUSTOMER, 35k DATASET, & NYSEG SCALE)
# ==============================================================================
plot3_data <- savings_df |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(per_cust_usd, dataset_35k_k, nyseg_total_m),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "val") |>
  mutate(
    metric = factor(metric,
                    levels = c("per_cust_usd", "dataset_35k_k", "nyseg_total_m"),
                    labels = c("Per Enrolled Customer ($/yr)",
                               "Full Dataset: 35k Custs ($K/yr)",
                               "NYSEG Total: 924.5k Custs ($M/yr)")),
    lbl = case_when(
      metric == "Per Enrolled Customer ($/yr)"   ~ dollar(val, accuracy = 1),
      metric == "Full Dataset: 35k Custs ($K/yr)" ~ paste0("$", comma(val, accuracy = 1), "K"),
      TRUE                                       ~ sprintf("$%.2fM", val)
    )
  )

p_savings <- ggplot(plot3_data, aes(x = val, y = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = lbl), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.6,
            fontface = "bold", color = "#1B2A4A") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x", ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = scen_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.28))) +
  labs(title = "Annual Customer Bill Savings Under TOU Pricing",
       subtitle = cap_sub_label,
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

```{r}
---
title: "price"
format: html
---

```{r}
# 1. Monthly NYSEG supply rates ($/kWh, West service area)
rates <- data.frame(
  month         = 1:12,
  rate_label    = c("Jan'26", "Feb'26", "Mar '26", "Apr'26", "May'26", "Jun'26",
                    "Jul'26", "Aug'26", "Sep'26", "Oct'25", "Nov'25", "Dec'25"),
  standard_rate = c(0.12, 0.11, 0.12, 0.15, 0.14, 0.09, 0.12, 0.07, 0.08, 0.10, 0.07, 0.10),
  off_peak_rate = c(0.18, 0.12, 0.07, 0.08, 0.08, 0.05, 0.08, 0.05, 0.04, 0.07, 0.06, 0.11),
  mid_peak_rate = c(0.21, 0.14, 0.09, 0.09, 0.12, 0.10, 0.14, 0.06, 0.07, 0.10, 0.08, 0.14),
  peak_rate     = c(0.26, 0.16, NA,   NA,   NA,   0.11, 0.17, 0.07, NA,   NA,   NA,   0.16),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# 2. Build 576-row grid (12 months x 2 day types x 24 hours)
df <- expand.grid(
  hour_ending = 1:24,
  day_type    = c("Weekday", "Weekend"),
  month       = 1:12,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df <- df[, c("month", "day_type", "hour_ending")]

# 3. Add month abbreviation, season, and readable clock interval
df$month_name <- month.abb[df$month]
df$season <- ifelse(df$month %in% c(12, 1, 2), "Winter",
             ifelse(df$month %in% c(3, 4, 5),  "Spring",
             ifelse(df$month %in% c(6, 7, 8),  "Summer", "Fall")))

start_h <- (df$hour_ending - 1) %% 24
end_h   <- df$hour_ending %% 24
fmt_hr  <- function(h) {
  ifelse(h == 0, "12:00 am",
  ifelse(h < 12, paste0(h, ":00 am"),
  ifelse(h == 12, "12:00 pm", paste0(h - 12, ":00 pm"))))
}
df$time_period <- paste0(fmt_hr(start_h), " - ", fmt_hr(end_h))

# 4. Assign TOU period (Off-peak, Mid-peak, Peak)
is_winter_fall <- df$season %in% c("Winter", "Fall")
is_off <- ifelse(is_winter_fall,
                 df$hour_ending == 24 | df$hour_ending %in% 1:7,
                 df$hour_ending %in% 1:8)

is_peak <- (df$day_type == "Weekday") & (
  (df$season == "Winter" & (df$hour_ending %in% 8:10 | df$hour_ending %in% 18:22)) |
  (df$season == "Summer" & (df$hour_ending %in% 12:19))
)

df$tou_period  <- ifelse(is_off, "Off-peak", ifelse(is_peak, "Peak", "Mid-peak"))
df$is_on_peak  <- as.integer(df$tou_period == "Peak")
df$is_off_peak <- as.integer(df$tou_period == "Off-peak")

# 5. Half-hour weights for 11:30 pm (Fall/Winter) and 12:30 am (Spring/Summer)
df$off_peak_frac <- ifelse(is_winter_fall & df$hour_ending %in% 1:7, 1.0,
                    ifelse(is_winter_fall & df$hour_ending == 24,    0.5,
                    ifelse(!is_winter_fall & df$hour_ending %in% 2:8, 1.0,
                    ifelse(!is_winter_fall & df$hour_ending == 1,     0.5, 0.0))))
df$peak_frac     <- as.numeric(df$tou_period == "Peak")
df$mid_peak_frac <- 1.0 - df$off_peak_frac - df$peak_frac

# 6. Merge monthly prices and calculate hourly $/kWh rates
df <- merge(df, rates, by = "month", all.x = TRUE)
df <- df[order(df$month, df$day_type, df$hour_ending), ]
rownames(df) <- NULL

df$tou_rate <- ifelse(df$tou_period == "Off-peak", df$off_peak_rate,
               ifelse(df$tou_period == "Mid-peak", df$mid_peak_rate, df$peak_rate))

peak_rate_zero <- ifelse(is.na(df$peak_rate), 0, df$peak_rate)
df$effective_tou_rate <- (df$off_peak_frac * df$off_peak_rate) +
                         (df$mid_peak_frac * df$mid_peak_rate) +
                         (df$peak_frac     * peak_rate_zero)

df

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(arrow)

# ==================================================================
# 1. Population proportions from cust_char
# 2. Representative sample of ~5,000 customers that matches the
#    JOINT distribution of the flags (not just each flag on its own)
# 3. Verify the sample, then cut ds down to just those customers
#
# Assumes `ds` (Arrow Dataset) and `cust_char` already exist. If cust_char
# is a csv, it is read below.
# ==================================================================

n_target         <- 5000
min_per_pattern  <- 5     # 0 = purely proportional. Set e.g. 5 to guarantee rare
                          # combinations at least a few customers (slightly distorts proportions)
restrict_to_ds   <- TRUE  # only sample customers that actually appear in ds
seed             <- 42

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Load and prepare
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if (!exists("cust_char")) {
  cust_char <- read.csv("cust_char.csv", colClasses = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER = "character"))
}
cust_char <- as_tibble(cust_char) |> mutate(CUSTOMER_NUMBER = as.character(CUSTOMER_NUMBER))
flags <- setdiff(names(cust_char), "CUSTOMER_NUMBER")

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(cust_char$CUSTOMER_NUMBER))
if (anyNA(cust_char[flags])) warning("Missing values in flag columns; rows with NA are dropped.")
cust <- cust_char |> filter(if_all(all_of(flags), ~ !is.na(.x)))

# Sampling from customers that have no usage data would be wasted effort
if (restrict_to_ds) {
  in_ds <- ds |> distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |> collect() |> pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |> as.character()
  cat("Customers in cust_char:", nrow(cust), " | also present in ds:", sum(cust$CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% in_ds), "\n")
  cust <- cust |> filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% in_ds)
}
N <- nrow(cust)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Population proportions
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
pop_props <- tibble(
  feature = flags,
  n       = colSums(cust[flags]),
  pct     = round(100 * colMeans(cust[flags]), 2)
)
cat("\nPopulation (N =", N, "):\n"); print(pop_props)

# Sanity checks on how the flags relate (adjust to what makes sense for your data)
cat("\nHow the flags overlap (top 15 combinations):\n")
cust <- cust |> mutate(pattern = do.call(paste, c(cust[flags], sep = "")))
pattern_tbl <- cust |>
  count(pattern, name = "n_pop") |>
  left_join(distinct(cust, pattern, across(all_of(flags))), by = "pattern") |>
  arrange(desc(n_pop)) |>
  mutate(pct_pop = round(100 * n_pop / N, 2))
print(head(pattern_tbl, 15), width = Inf)
cat("Distinct flag combinations:", nrow(pattern_tbl), "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Stratified sample: allocate n_target across flag combinations in
#    proportion to how common each is (largest-remainder rounding so the
#    total is exactly n_target)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
n_target <- min(n_target, N)

allocate <- function(n_pat, total, minimum) {
  guaranteed <- pmin(n_pat, minimum)
  remaining  <- total - sum(guaranteed)
  stopifnot(remaining >= 0)
  room  <- n_pat - guaranteed
  exact <- room / sum(room) * remaining
  base  <- floor(exact)
  extra <- remaining - sum(base)
  if (extra > 0) {
    idx <- order(exact - base, decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(extra)]
    base[idx] <- base[idx] + 1
  }
  pmin(guaranteed + base, n_pat)
}

pattern_tbl$n_take <- allocate(pattern_tbl$n_pop, n_target, min_per_pattern)

set.seed(seed)
sample_ids <- cust |>
  inner_join(select(pattern_tbl, pattern, n_take), by = "pattern") |>
  group_by(pattern) |>
  slice(sample.int(n(), first(n_take))) |>
  ungroup()

cat("\nSample size:", nrow(sample_ids), "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Verify the sample matches the population
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
check <- tibble(
  feature    = flags,
  pop_pct    = round(100 * colMeans(cust[flags]), 2),
  sample_pct = round(100 * colMeans(sample_ids[flags]), 2),
  sample_n   = colSums(sample_ids[flags])
) |> mutate(diff_pts = round(sample_pct - pop_pct, 2))
cat("\nMarginal check (difference should be near 0):\n"); print(check)

joint <- pattern_tbl |>
  transmute(pattern, pop_pct = 100 * n_pop / N, sample_pct = 100 * n_take / nrow(sample_ids))
tv_distance <- 0.5 * sum(abs(joint$pop_pct - joint$sample_pct)) / 100
cat("\nJoint-pattern total variation distance:", round(tv_distance, 4),
    "(0 = identical distribution)\n")
cat("Combinations with zero customers in the sample:", sum(pattern_tbl$n_take == 0),
    "(these make up", round(sum(pattern_tbl$pct_pop[pattern_tbl$n_take == 0]), 2), "% of the population)\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Save the sample and cut ds down to those customers
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
write.csv(select(sample_ids, -pattern), "cust_char_sample.csv", row.names = FALSE)

ids <- sample_ids$CUSTOMER_NUMBER
ds |>
  filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% ids) |>
  write_dataset("ds_sample", format = "parquet")   # one pass over the full data

ds_s <- open_dataset("ds_sample")
cat("\nRows in sample dataset:", format(nrow(ds_s), big.mark = ","), "\n")
# From here on, use ds_s in place of ds in your other scripts.


proportion = mean(c(1.11, 1.47,1.08))


```

```{r}
library(arrow)
library(dplyr)
library(cli)

# ==================================================================
# Builds `sub_df`: one row per customer x month x day_type x hour_ending
# with summed kWh, number of hours observed, and the rate columns.
#
# Needs two things to exist first:
#   ds  (or ds_s, the sampled dataset from sample_customers.R)
#   df  (the 576-row TOU rate grid from your rate-table script)
# ==================================================================

stopifnot("Run your rate-grid script first so `df` exists" = exists("df"))

src <- if (exists("ds_s")) ds_s else ds     # use the 5k sample if you made one
cat("Source:", if (exists("ds_s")) "ds_s (sample)" else "ds (full)", "\n")

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Months in the data
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
months <- src |>
  transmute(ym = substr(usage_date, 1, 7)) |>
  distinct() |>
  collect() |>
  pull(ym) |>
  sort()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Aggregate one month at a time inside Arrow (progress bar + resume)
#    One pass per month, instead of looping over customer batches.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
dir.create("ckpt_subdf", showWarnings = FALSE)
pb <- cli_progress_bar(
  "Building sub_df", total = length(months),
  format = "{pb_spin} {pb_bar} {pb_percent} | {pb_current}/{pb_total} months | ETA {pb_eta} | {pb_status}"
)

for (i in seq_along(months)) {
  ym <- months[i]
  f  <- file.path("ckpt_subdf", paste0(ym, ".rds"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) {
    lo <- paste0(ym, "-01"); hi <- paste0(ym, "-31")
    out <- src |>
      filter(
        usage_date >= lo, usage_date <= hi,
        !is.na(CUSTOMER_NUMBER),
        as.integer(is_complete_hour) == 1,
        !is.na(hourly_kwh)
      ) |>
      mutate(
        month       = as.integer(substr(usage_date, 6, 7)),
        hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending),
        hourly_kwh  = as.numeric(hourly_kwh)
      ) |>
      group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending) |>
      summarise(n_hours = n(), hourly_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh)) |>
      collect() |>
      ungroup()
    saveRDS(out, f)
  }
  cli_progress_update(id = pb, set = i, status = ym)
}
cli_progress_done(id = pb)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Combine, normalize day_type, join the rates, compute costs
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
sub_df <- bind_rows(lapply(file.path("ckpt_subdf", paste0(months, ".rds")), readRDS)) |>
  mutate(
    CUSTOMER_NUMBER = as.integer(CUSTOMER_NUMBER),
    day_type = if_else(grepl("^weekend", day_type, ignore.case = TRUE), "Weekend", "Weekday")
  ) |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending) |>
  summarise(n_hours = sum(n_hours), hourly_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period, standard_rate, tou_rate, effective_tou_rate),
    by = c("month", "day_type", "hour_ending")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    cost_standard = hourly_kwh * standard_rate,
    cost_tou      = hourly_kwh * tou_rate
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Checks
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
cat("\nsub_df:", format(nrow(sub_df), big.mark = ","), "rows,",
    n_distinct(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER), "customers\n")
cat("Rows with no rate match (should be 0):", sum(is.na(sub_df$tou_period)), "\n")
print(sub_df |> count(day_type))
print(sub_df |> distinct(month) |> arrange(month) |> pull(month))   # months present

saveRDS(sub_df, "sub_df.rds")   # reload later with: sub_df <- readRDS("sub_df.rds")

```

library(dplyr)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. CUSTOMER-LEVEL SUMMARY (1 ROW PER CUSTOMER OVER THE YEAR)
# ==============================================================================
cust_summary <- sub_df |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    n_hours             = sum(n_hours),
    total_kwh           = sum(hourly_kwh),
    kwh_off_peak        = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Off-peak"]),
    kwh_mid_peak        = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Mid-peak"]),
    kwh_peak            = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"]),
    pct_kwh_off_peak    = if_else(total_kwh > 0, kwh_off_peak / total_kwh * 100, 0),
    pct_kwh_mid_peak    = if_else(total_kwh > 0, kwh_mid_peak / total_kwh * 100, 0),
    pct_kwh_peak        = if_else(total_kwh > 0, kwh_peak     / total_kwh * 100, 0),
    total_paid_standard = sum(cost_standard),
    total_paid_tou      = sum(cost_tou),
    paid_off_peak       = sum(cost_tou[tou_period == "Off-peak"]),
    paid_mid_peak       = sum(cost_tou[tou_period == "Mid-peak"]),
    paid_peak           = sum(cost_tou[tou_period == "Peak"]),
    tou_savings         = total_paid_standard - total_paid_tou,
    tou_savings_pct     = if_else(total_paid_standard > 0, (tou_savings / total_paid_standard) * 100, 0),
    .groups             = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

cust_summary

# ==============================================================================
# 2. COHORT-WIDE SUMMARY ACROSS ALL CUSTOMERS (TOTAL, MEAN, MEDIAN, RANGE)
# ==============================================================================
cohort_summary <- tibble(
  metric = c("total_kwh", "total_paid_standard", "total_paid_tou", "tou_savings"),
  vals   = list(
    cust_summary$total_kwh,
    cust_summary$total_paid_standard,
    cust_summary$total_paid_tou,
    cust_summary$tou_savings
  )
) |>
  rowwise() |>
  summarise(
    metric      = metric,
    n_customers = length(vals),
    total       = sum(vals),
    mean        = mean(vals),
    median      = median(vals),
    min         = min(vals),
    max         = max(vals),
    range       = max(vals) - min(vals),
    .groups     = "drop"
  )

cohort_summary

n_total_custs <- n_distinct(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

tou_category_summary <- sub_df |>
  group_by(tou_period) |>
  summarise(
    total_hours             = sum(n_hours),
    total_kwh               = sum(hourly_kwh),
    total_mwh               = sum(hourly_kwh) / 1000,

    pct_of_tou_bill = total_paid_tou / sum(total_paid_tou) * 100
  ) |>
  select(
    tou_period,
    total_hours, pct_of_hours,
    total_kwh, total_mwh, pct_of_kwh,
    avg_kw_per_hour, avg_annual_kwh_per_cust,
    total_paid_tou, pct_of_tou_bill
  ) |>
  arrange(factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak")))

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Attach seasonal labels matching the TOU schedule (Winter: Dec-Feb, Spring: Mar-May, Summer: Jun-Aug, Fall: Sep-Nov)
sub_df_season <- sub_df |>
  mutate(
    season = factor(
      case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
        month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring",
        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall"
      ),
      levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")
    )
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 2. COHORT-WIDE SUMMARY BY SEASON (TOTAL, MEAN, MEDIAN, MIN, MAX, RANGE)
# ==============================================================================
cust_seasonal <- sub_df_season |>
  group_by(season, CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    total_kwh           = sum(hourly_kwh),
    total_paid_standard = sum(cost_standard),
    total_paid_tou      = sum(cost_tou),
    tou_savings         = total_paid_standard - total_paid_tou,
    .groups             = "drop"
  )

cohort_summary_season <- cust_seasonal |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(total_kwh, total_paid_standard, total_paid_tou, tou_savings),
    names_to  = "metric",
    values_to = "val"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    metric = factor(
      metric,
      levels = c("total_kwh", "total_paid_standard", "total_paid_tou", "tou_savings")
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(season, metric) |>
  summarise(
    n_customers = n(),
    total       = sum(val),
    mean        = mean(val),
    median      = median(val),
    min         = min(val),
    max         = max(val),
    range       = max(val) - min(val),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(season, metric)

cohort_summary_season

# ==============================================================================
# 3. TOU CATEGORIZATION BREAKDOWN BY SEASON (kWh, kW & $ IN EACH TIER)
# ==============================================================================
tou_category_season <- sub_df_season |>
  group_by(season, tou_period) |>
  summarise(
    n_customers      = n_distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER),
    total_hours      = sum(n_hours),
    total_kwh        = sum(hourly_kwh),
    total_mwh        = sum(hourly_kwh) / 1000,
    avg_kw_per_hour  = sum(hourly_kwh) / sum(n_hours),
    avg_kwh_per_cust = sum(hourly_kwh) / n_customers,
    total_paid_tou   = sum(cost_tou),
    .groups          = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(season) |>
  mutate(
    pct_of_season_hours    = total_hours    / sum(total_hours)    * 100,
    pct_of_season_kwh      = total_kwh      / sum(total_kwh)      * 100,
    pct_of_season_tou_bill = total_paid_tou / sum(total_paid_tou) * 100
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(
    season, tou_period,
    total_hours, pct_of_season_hours,
    total_kwh, total_mwh, pct_of_season_kwh,
    avg_kw_per_hour, avg_kwh_per_cust,
    total_paid_tou, pct_of_season_tou_bill
  ) |>
  arrange(season, factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak")))

library(dplyr)

# ==============================================================================

hourly_season_df <- sub_df |>

  mutate(

      case_when(

        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)"
      ),
      levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Spring (Mar–May)",
                 "Summer (Jun–Aug)", "Fall (Sep–Nov)")
    ),
    tou_period = factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak"))
  ) |>
  group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
  summarise(
    total_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh),

# ==============================================================================

)

p_seasonal_ts <- ggplot() +

  ) +

    data = shade_blocks,

    fontface = "bold",

  ) +

    breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,

  labs(

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. RANDOMLY SELECT 2% OF ALL CUSTOMERS FOR ENPHASE IQ BATTERY 10C (2 UNITS)
# ==============================================================================
set.seed(42)
all_custs <- unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
battery_custs <- sample(all_custs, size = round(0.02 * length(all_custs)))

# Enphase IQ Battery 10C (2-unit setup) specs
cap_kwh    <- 20.16          # Total usable energy capacity (kWh)
max_kw     <- 7.68           # Continuous grid charge/discharge power limit (kW)
rt_eff     <- 0.894          # Round-trip efficiency (89.4%)
eta        <- sqrt(rt_eff)   # One-way charge/discharge efficiency (~0.9455)
taper_frac <- 0.45           # Tapering off-peak charge rate (45% of remaining empty capacity/hr)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. VECTORIZED 24-HOUR DISPATCH SIMULATION FOR THE 5% BATTERY FLEET
#    - Charges during Off-peak (tapering as battery fills, capped at 7.68 kW)
#    - Discharges during Peak (Winter/Summer) or Mid-peak (Spring/Fall, no Peak tier)
#    - Strictly bounded by stored state of charge (cannot discharge more than stored)
# ==============================================================================
bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
  filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs) |>
  mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
  select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
  complete(
    nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
    hour_ending = 1:24,
    fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)
  ) |>
  arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

# Wide matrix of baseline hourly kW: rows = (customer x month x day_type), cols = HE 1..24
kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols     = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
    names_from  = hour_ending,
    values_from = avg_kw_before
  )

kw_mat <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
n_prof <- nrow(kw_mat)

# Matching matrix of TOU periods ("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak") for each row & hour
per_wide <- kw_wide |>
  select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
  left_join(
    df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
    by = c("month", "day_type"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols     = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
    names_from  = hour_ending,
    values_from = tou_period
  )

per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])

# Discharge in Peak when Peak exists (Winter/Summer weekdays); otherwise discharge in Mid-peak
has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0

soc     <- rep(0, n_prof)
out_mat <- kw_mat

# Run 2 consecutive 24-hr cycles so midnight wrap-around reaches steady state on pass 2
for (pass in 1:2) {
  for (h in 1:24) {
    l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0)
    p <- per_mat[, h]

    # Charge in Off-peak up to 7.68 kW and remaining battery capacity
    is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
    grid_charge <- ifelse(
      is_charge,
      pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta),
      0
    )
    soc <- soc + (grid_charge * eta)

    # Discharge once Peak starts (or Mid-peak in Spring/Fall), strictly <= stored energy
    is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
                    (soc > 0) & (l > 0)
    deliver <- ifelse(
      is_discharge,
      pmin(l, max_kw, soc * eta),
      0
    )
    soc <- soc - (deliver / eta)

    if (pass == 2) {
      out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
    }
  }
}

# Reshape simulated post-battery hourly kW back to long format & join onto full fleet
bat_after_long <- bind_cols(
  kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
  as_tibble(out_mat)
) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = as.character(1:24),
    names_to  = "hour_ending",
    values_to = "avg_kw_after"
  ) |>
  mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

sim_sub_df <- sub_df |>
  left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
  mutate(
    has_battery  = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs,
    kwh_before   = hourly_kwh,
    kwh_after    = if_else(has_battery, avg_kw_after * n_hours, hourly_kwh),
    cost_before  = kwh_before * tou_rate,
    cost_after   = kwh_after  * tou_rate
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 3. QUICK CHECK: ENERGY CONSERVATION & SHIFT ACROSS TOU PERIODS (FULL FLEET)
# ==============================================================================
shift_check <- sim_sub_df |>
  group_by(tou_period) |>
  summarise(
    mwh_before     = sum(kwh_before) / 1000,
    mwh_after      = sum(kwh_after)  / 1000,
    mwh_diff       = mwh_after - mwh_before,
    pct_change     = (mwh_after - mwh_before) / mwh_before * 100,
    .groups        = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak")))

shift_check

# ==============================================================================
# 4. REPLOT SEASONAL WEEKDAY TIME SERIES: BEFORE vs. AFTER 5% BATTERY ROLLOUT
# ==============================================================================
hourly_season_sim <- sim_sub_df |>
  filter(day_type == "Weekday") |>
  mutate(
    season = factor(
      case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)",
        month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring (Mar–May)",
        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)"
      ),
      levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Spring (Mar–May)",
                 "Summer (Jun–Aug)", "Fall (Sep–Nov)")
    ),
    tou_period = factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak"))
  ) |>
  group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
  summarise(
    Before = sum(kwh_before) / 1000,
    After  = sum(kwh_after)  / 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(season, hour_ending)

# Shaded TOU background blocks & direct labels
shade_blocks <- hourly_season_sim |>
  group_by(season) |>
  mutate(block_id = cumsum(tou_period != lag(tou_period, default = first(tou_period)))) |>
  group_by(season, block_id, tou_period) |>
  summarise(
    xmin  = min(hour_ending) - 1,
    xmax  = max(hour_ending),
    mid_x = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    label = if_else((xmax - xmin) >= 2, as.character(first(tou_period)), ""),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Long format for plotting Before vs. After lines cleanly with a legend
lines_df <- hourly_season_sim |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(Before, After),
    names_to  = "scenario",
    values_to = "total_mwh"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    scenario = factor(
      scenario,
      levels = c("Before", "After"),
      labels = c("Before Battery (Baseline)", "After Battery (5% Fleet Adoption)")
    )
  )

tou_colors <- c(
  "Off-peak" = "#0077C8",
  "Mid-peak" = "#00853E",
  "Peak"     = "#B57A14"
)

p_sim_ts <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = shade_blocks,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tou_period),
    alpha = 0.18
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = shade_blocks,
    aes(x = mid_x, y = Inf, label = label, color = tou_period),
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = lines_df,
    aes(x = hour_ending - 0.5, y = total_mwh, linetype = scenario, linewidth = scenario),
    color = "#1B2A4A"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = lines_df,
    aes(x = hour_ending - 0.5, y = total_mwh, shape = scenario),
    color = "#1B2A4A",
    size = 1.8
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tou_colors, name = "TOU Window") +
  scale_color_manual(values = tou_colors, guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(
    values = c("Before Battery (Baseline)" = "solid", "After Battery (5% Fleet Adoption)" = "dashed"),
    name = "Fleet Scenario"
  ) +
  scale_linewidth_manual(
    values = c("Before Battery (Baseline)" = 1.0, "After Battery (5% Fleet Adoption)" = 1.15),
    name = "Fleet Scenario"
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Before Battery (Baseline)" = 16, "After Battery (5% Fleet Adoption)" = 17),
    name = "Fleet Scenario"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
    labels = c("12am", "4am", "8am", "12pm", "4pm", "8pm", "12am"),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.22))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Fleet Load Shift After Deploying Enphase IQ Battery 10C to 5% of Customers",
    subtitle = "Batteries charge overnight in Off-peak (20.16 kWh cap, 7.68 kW max, 89.4% RTE) and shave Peak / Mid-peak demand",
    x = "Time of Day",
    y = "Total Weekday Usage (MWh)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.position  = "top",
    legend.box       = "vertical",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing    = unit(1.1, "lines")
  )

p_sim_ts

library(dplyr)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. ENSURE SEASONAL CUSTOMER BILLS EXIST (USES cust_seasonal OR BUILDS FROM sub_df)
# ==============================================================================
if (!exists("cust_seasonal")) {
  cust_seasonal <- sub_df |>
    mutate(
      season = factor(
        case_when(
          month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
          month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring",
          month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer",
          TRUE                   ~ "Fall"
        ),
        levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")
      )
    ) |>
    group_by(season, CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(
      total_kwh           = sum(hourly_kwh),
      total_paid_standard = sum(cost_standard),
      total_paid_tou      = sum(cost_tou),
      tou_savings         = total_paid_standard - total_paid_tou,
      .groups             = "drop"
    )
}

# ==============================================================================
# 2. MAP CUSTOMERS TO THEIR CATEGORIES IN cust_char & COMPUTE SEASONAL MEANS
# ==============================================================================
cat_labels <- c(
  "is_solar"                 = "Solar",
  "lvl1EV"                   = "Level 1 EV",
  "lvl2EV"                   = "Level 2 EV",
  "heatpump"                 = "Heat Pump",
  "AC"                       = "AC",
  "no_electric_temp_control" = "No Electric Temp Control",
  "high_overall_use"     = "High Overall Use",
  "peak_demand_contributor"  = "Peak Demand Contributor"
)

cust_long_cats <- cust_char |>
  mutate(CUSTOMER_NUMBER = as.integer(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(names(cat_labels)),
    names_to  = "raw_category",
    values_to = "has_feature"
  ) |>
  filter(as.integer(has_feature) == 1) |>
  mutate(
    category = factor(
      cat_labels[raw_category],
      levels = unname(cat_labels)
    )
  ) |>
  select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, category)

# Summary table by category and season
cat_season_summary <- cust_long_cats |>
  inner_join(cust_seasonal, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(category, season) |>
  summarise(
    n_customers  = n_distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER),
    mean_savings = mean(tou_savings, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_savings  = median(tou_savings, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(category) |>
  mutate(
    facet_label = sprintf("%s\n(n = %s)", category, comma(max(n_customers)))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    facet_label = factor(facet_label, levels = unique(facet_label[order(category)])),
    direction   = if_else(mean_savings >= 0, "Saves on TOU", "Costs More on TOU")
  )

cat_season_summary

# ==============================================================================

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. RECALCULATE SEASONAL BILLS WITH FULL SUPPLY + DELIVERY PRICING
#    - TOU (SC12): Supply (tou_rate)      + $0.07011/kWh delivery + $30/month
#    - Standard:   Supply (standard_rate) + $0.09138/kWh delivery + $19/month
# ==============================================================================
tou_deliv_kwh <- 0.07011
tou_fixed_mo  <- 30.00

std_deliv_kwh <- 0.09138
std_fixed_mo  <- 19.00

cust_seasonal_full <- sub_df |>
  mutate(
    season = factor(
      case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter",
        month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring",
        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall"
      ),
      levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")
    ),
    full_cost_standard = hourly_kwh * (standard_rate + std_deliv_kwh),
    full_cost_tou      = hourly_kwh * (tou_rate      + tou_deliv_kwh)
  ) |>
  group_by(season, CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    n_months            = n_distinct(month),
    total_kwh           = sum(hourly_kwh),
    total_paid_standard = sum(full_cost_standard) + (std_fixed_mo * n_months),
    total_paid_tou      = sum(full_cost_tou)      + (tou_fixed_mo * n_months),
    tou_savings         = total_paid_standard - total_paid_tou,
    .groups             = "drop"
  )

# Track annual kWh per customer to flag NYSEG's 35,000 kWh/year SC12 eligibility rule
cust_annual_kwh <- cust_seasonal_full |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    annual_kwh       = sum(total_kwh),
    is_sc12_eligible = annual_kwh >= 35000,
    .groups          = "drop"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 2. MAP CUSTOMERS TO cust_char CATEGORIES & COMPUTE SEASONAL MEANS
# ==============================================================================
cat_labels <- c(
  "is_solar"                 = "Solar",
  "lvl1EV"                   = "Level 1 EV",
  "lvl2EV"                   = "Level 2 EV",
  "heatpump"                 = "Heat Pump",
  "AC"                       = "AC",
  "no_electric_temp_control" = "No Electric Temp Control",
  "high_overall_use"     = "High Overall Use",
  "peak_demand_contributor"  = "Peak Demand Contributor"
)


cust_long_cats <- cust_char |>
  mutate(CUSTOMER_NUMBER = as.integer(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = all_of(names(cat_labels)),
    names_to  = "raw_category",
    values_to = "has_feature"
  ) |>
  filter(as.integer(has_feature) == 1) |>
  mutate(
    category = factor(
      cat_labels[raw_category],
      levels = unname(cat_labels)
    )
  ) |>
  select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, category)

cat_season_summary <- cust_long_cats |>
  inner_join(cust_seasonal_full, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  left_join(cust_annual_kwh, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER") |>
  group_by(category, season) |>
  summarise(
    n_customers      = n_distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER),
    pct_sc12_elig    = mean(is_sc12_eligible) * 100,
    mean_season_kwh  = mean(total_kwh),
    mean_savings     = mean(tou_savings, na.rm = TRUE),
    med_savings      = median(tou_savings, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups          = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(category) |>
  mutate(
    facet_label = sprintf("%s\n(n = %s)", category, comma(max(n_customers)))
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    facet_label = factor(facet_label, levels = unique(facet_label[order(category)])),
    direction   = if_else(mean_savings >= 0, "Saves on TOU", "Costs More on TOU")
  )

cat_season_summary

# ==============================================================================
# 3. REPLOT SEASONAL FULL-BILL SAVINGS BY CUSTOMER CATEGORY
# ==============================================================================
p_cat_savings_full <- ggplot(cat_season_summary, aes(x = season, y = mean_savings, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.58) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.55, color = "grey30") +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = sprintf("%s$%.2f", if_else(mean_savings >= 0, "+", "-"), abs(mean_savings)),
      vjust = if_else(mean_savings >= 0, -0.45, 1.35)
    ),
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.1
  ) +
