library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. COMPUTE CUSTOMER VOLUME, PERSISTENT PEAK kW, AND SPIKINESS FROM sub_df
# ==============================================================================
cust_load_metrics <- sub_df |>
  mutate(avg_kw = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    total_hours        = sum(n_hours),
    annual_kwh         = sum(hourly_kwh),
    mean_annual_kw     = if_else(total_hours > 0, annual_kwh / total_hours, 0),
    peak_kwh           = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"]),
    pct_kwh_peak       = if_else(annual_kwh > 0, peak_kwh / annual_kwh * 100, 0),
    mean_peak_kw       = if_else(
      sum(n_hours[tou_period == "Peak"]) > 0,
      peak_kwh / sum(n_hours[tou_period == "Peak"]),
      0
    ),
    # Highest recurring monthly-hourly average kW during NYSEG Peak windows
    persistent_peak_kw = max(avg_kw[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
    # Spikiness ratio: how much higher peak draw is than year-round average draw
    peak_to_avg_ratio  = if_else(mean_annual_kw > 0, persistent_peak_kw / mean_annual_kw, 0),
    .groups            = "drop"
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 2. JOIN cust_char FLAGS & ASSIGN MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ACTIONABLE SEGMENTS
# ==============================================================================
peak_kw_cutoff <- quantile(cust_load_metrics$persistent_peak_kw, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)

cust_segments <- cust_load_metrics |>
  left_join(
    cust_char |> mutate(CUSTOMER_NUMBER = as.integer(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)),
    by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    is_tou_eligible = annual_kwh >= 35000,
    is_high_peak    = (coalesce(peak_demand_contributor, 0) == 1) |
                      (persistent_peak_kw >= peak_kw_cutoff),
    has_flex_tech   = (coalesce(lvl1EV, 0) == 1) |
                      (coalesce(lvl2EV, 0) == 1) |
                      (coalesce(heatpump, 0) == 1) |
                      (coalesce(AC, 0) == 1) |
                      (coalesce(is_solar, 0) == 1),
    segment = case_when(
      is_tou_eligible ~
        "1. TOU-Eligible High Volume (>=35k kWh)",
      !is_tou_eligible & is_high_peak ~
        "2. Non-TOU Prime Battery Target (<35k kWh, High Peak)",
      !is_tou_eligible & !is_high_peak & has_flex_tech ~
        "3. Non-TOU Flexible Tech (<35k kWh, EV/HVAC/Solar)",
      TRUE ~
        "4. Non-TOU Low / Flat Load (<35k kWh, Baseline)"
    ),
    segment = factor(
      segment,
      levels = c(
        "1. TOU-Eligible High Volume (>=35k kWh)",
        "2. Non-TOU Prime Battery Target (<35k kWh, High Peak)",
        "3. Non-TOU Flexible Tech (<35k kWh, EV/HVAC/Solar)",
        "4. Non-TOU Low / Flat Load (<35k kWh, Baseline)"
      )
    )
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 3. SEGMENT SUMMARY TABLE (SIZE, PEAK CONTRIBUTION & DEVICE BREAKDOWN)
# ==============================================================================
segment_summary <- cust_segments |>
  group_by(segment) |>
  summarise(
    n_customers           = n(),
    pct_of_customers      = n() / nrow(cust_segments) * 100,
    pct_of_fleet_peak_kwh = sum(peak_kwh) / sum(cust_segments$peak_kwh) * 100,
    median_annual_kwh     = median(annual_kwh),
    mean_persistent_pk_kw = mean(persistent_peak_kw),
    mean_spikiness_ratio  = mean(peak_to_avg_ratio),
    pct_ev                = mean(coalesce(lvl1EV, 0) == 1 | coalesce(lvl2EV, 0) == 1) * 100,
    pct_heatpump          = mean(coalesce(heatpump, 0) == 1) * 100,
    pct_ac                = mean(coalesce(AC, 0) == 1) * 100,
    pct_solar             = mean(coalesce(is_solar, 0) == 1) * 100,
    .groups               = "drop"
  )

segment_summary

# ==============================================================================
# 4. QUADRANT SCATTER PLOT: UNCOVERING NON-TOU BATTERY CANDIDATES
# ==============================================================================
seg_colors <- c(
  "1. TOU-Eligible High Volume (>=35k kWh)"              = "#00853E",
  "2. Non-TOU Prime Battery Target (<35k kWh, High Peak)" = "#D97706",
  "3. Non-TOU Flexible Tech (<35k kWh, EV/HVAC/Solar)"   = "#0077C8",
  "4. Non-TOU Low / Flat Load (<35k kWh, Baseline)"      = "#9CA3AF"
)
# Set x-axis ceiling high enough to show the 35,000 kWh SC12 threshold and green points
x_max <- max(45000, quantile(cust_segments$annual_kwh, 0.998, na.rm = TRUE))
y_max <- quantile(cust_segments$persistent_peak_kw, 0.998, na.rm = TRUE)

p_seg_quadrant <- ggplot(
  cust_segments,
  aes(x = annual_kwh, y = persistent_peak_kw, color = segment)
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 35000, linetype = "dashed", color = "#1B2A4A", linewidth = 0.85) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = peak_kw_cutoff, linetype = "dotted", color = "#B57A14", linewidth = 0.85) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = 35000, y = y_max * 0.95,
    label = "NYSEG SC12 TOU Minimum (35,000 kWh/yr) →",
    hjust = 1.03, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold",
    fill = "white", color = "#1B2A4A"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = 500, y = peak_kw_cutoff,
    label = sprintf("Top 10%% Persistent Peak Threshold (%.2f kW)", peak_kw_cutoff),
    hjust = 0, vjust = -0.4, size = 3.1, fontface = "bold",
    fill = "white", color = "#B57A14"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = seg_colors, name = "Customer Segment") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, x_max), ylim = c(0, y_max)) +
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1, size = 3.5), ncol = 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Customer Segmentation: Separating SC12 TOU Eligibility from Battery Peak Candidates",
    subtitle = "Upper-left quadrant (<35,000 kWh/yr but high recurring peak kW) identifies prime BESS targets locked out of SC12",
    x = "Annual Electricity Usage (kWh / Year)",
    y = "Persistent Peak-Window Demand (kW)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12.5) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position  = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. REUSABLE VECTORIZED ENPHASE IQ BATTERY 10C DISPATCH FUNCTION
# ==============================================================================
simulate_bess_fleet <- function(sub_df, df, battery_cust_ids,
                                cap_kwh = 20.16,
                                max_kw = 7.68,
                                rt_eff = 0.894,
                                taper_frac = 0.45) {
  eta <- sqrt(rt_eff)

  bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
    filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_cust_ids) |>
    mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
    complete(
      nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
      hour_ending = 1:24,
      fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)
    ) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

  kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
    pivot_wider(
      id_cols     = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
      names_from  = hour_ending,
      values_from = avg_kw_before
    ) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type)

  per_wide <- kw_wide |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
    left_join(
      df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
      by = c("month", "day_type"),
      relationship = "many-to-many"
    ) |>
    pivot_wider(
      id_cols     = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
      names_from  = hour_ending,
      values_from = tou_period
    ) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type)

  kw_mat  <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  n_prof  <- nrow(kw_mat)

  # Discharge during Peak (Winter/Summer) or Mid-peak (Spring/Fall when no Peak exists)
  has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0
  soc     <- rep(0, n_prof)
  out_mat <- kw_mat

  # 2 consecutive 24-hr passes so midnight wrap-around reaches steady state
  for (pass in 1:2) {
    for (h in 1:24) {
      l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0)
      p <- per_mat[, h]

      is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
      grid_charge <- ifelse(
        is_charge,
        pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta),
        0
      )
      soc <- soc + (grid_charge * eta)

      is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
                      (soc > 0) & (l > 0)
      deliver <- ifelse(is_discharge, pmin(l, max_kw, soc * eta), 0)
      soc     <- soc - (deliver / eta)

      if (pass == 2) {
        out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
      }
    }
  }

  bat_after_long <- bind_cols(
    kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
    as_tibble(out_mat)
  ) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols      = as.character(1:24),
      names_to  = "hour_ending",
      values_to = "avg_kw_after"
    ) |>
    mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

  sub_df |>
    left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    mutate(
      kwh_after = if_else(
        CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_cust_ids,
        avg_kw_after * n_hours,
        hourly_kwh
      )
    ) |>
    pull(kwh_after)
}

# ==============================================================================
# 2. DEFINE COHORTS: RANDOM 5% vs. TARGETED SEGMENT 2 (SAME 5% BATTERY BUDGET)
# ==============================================================================
set.seed(42)
all_custs <- unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
n_bats    <- round(0.05 * length(all_custs))

# Cohort A: Random 5% across entire fleet
random_5pct_custs <- sample(all_custs, size = n_bats)

# Cohort B: Top Segment 2 customers (<35k kWh/yr, High Peak) up to the same 5% budget
seg2_ranked <- cust_segments |>
  filter(grepl("^2\\.", segment)) |>
  arrange(desc(persistent_peak_kw))

targeted_seg2_5pct_custs <- seg2_ranked |>
  slice_head(n = min(n_bats, nrow(seg2_ranked))) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

# Cohort C (for table comparison): 100% of Segment 2 customers
all_seg2_custs <- seg2_ranked |> pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

# Run simulations
sim_all <- sub_df |>
  mutate(
    kwh_baseline      = hourly_kwh,
    kwh_random_5pct   = simulate_bess_fleet(sub_df, df, random_5pct_custs),
    kwh_targeted_5pct = simulate_bess_fleet(sub_df, df, targeted_seg2_5pct_custs),
    kwh_all_seg2      = simulate_bess_fleet(sub_df, df, all_seg2_custs)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 3. PER-BATTERY PERFORMANCE TABLE: RANDOM 5% vs. TARGETED SEGMENT 2
# ==============================================================================
calc_bess_efficiency <- function(df_sim, col_name, label, n_units) {
  peak_rows <- df_sim |> filter(tou_period == "Peak")
  wkday_peak_rows <- df_sim |> filter(tou_period == "Peak", day_type == "Weekday")

  base_peak_kwh   <- sum(peak_rows$kwh_baseline)
  sim_peak_kwh    <- sum(peak_rows[[col_name]])
  shaved_peak_kwh <- base_peak_kwh - sim_peak_kwh

  base_wkday_kw   <- sum(wkday_peak_rows$kwh_baseline) / sum(wkday_peak_rows$n_hours)
  sim_wkday_kw    <- sum(wkday_peak_rows[[col_name]])  / sum(wkday_peak_rows$n_hours)
  shaved_fleet_kw <- (sum(wkday_peak_rows$kwh_baseline) - sum(wkday_peak_rows[[col_name]])) /
                     (sum(wkday_peak_rows$n_hours) / n_distinct(df_sim$CUSTOMER_NUMBER))

  tibble(
    strategy                            = label,
    batteries_deployed                  = n_units,
    annual_peak_mwh_shaved              = shaved_peak_kwh / 1000,
    annual_peak_kwh_shaved_per_battery  = shaved_peak_kwh / n_units,
    avg_wkday_peak_kw_shaved_per_bat    = shaved_fleet_kw / n_units,
    fleet_peak_kwh_reduction_pct        = (shaved_peak_kwh / base_peak_kwh) * 100
  )
}

battery_efficiency_comparison <- bind_rows(
  calc_bess_efficiency(sim_all, "kwh_random_5pct",   "Random 5% Rollout",                length(random_5pct_custs)),
  calc_bess_efficiency(sim_all, "kwh_targeted_5pct", "Targeted 5% Rollout (Segment 2)",  length(targeted_seg2_5pct_custs)),
  calc_bess_efficiency(sim_all, "kwh_all_seg2",      "Full Segment 2 Rollout (100% S2)", length(all_seg2_custs))
)

battery_efficiency_comparison

# ==============================================================================
# 4. OVERLAID SEASONAL TIME-SERIES PLOT (ALL THREE SCENARIOS)
# ==============================================================================
hourly_overlay <- sim_all |>
  filter(day_type == "Weekday") |>
  mutate(
    season = factor(
      case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)",
        month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring (Mar–May)",
        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)"
      ),
      levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Spring (Mar–May)",
                 "Summer (Jun–Aug)", "Fall (Sep–Nov)")
    ),
    tou_period = factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak"))
  ) |>
  group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
  summarise(
    `Baseline (No Batteries)`           = sum(kwh_baseline)      / 1000,
    `Random 5% Rollout`                 = sum(kwh_random_5pct)   / 1000,
    `Targeted 5% Rollout (Segment 2)`   = sum(kwh_targeted_5pct) / 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(season, hour_ending)

tou_colors <- c(
  "Off-peak" = "#0077C8",
  "Mid-peak" = "#00853E",
  "Peak"     = "#B57A14"
)

shade_blocks <- hourly_overlay |>
  group_by(season) |>
  mutate(block_id = cumsum(tou_period != lag(tou_period, default = first(tou_period)))) |>
  group_by(season, block_id, tou_period) |>
  summarise(
    xmin      = min(hour_ending) - 1,
    xmax      = max(hour_ending),
    mid_x     = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    label     = if_else((xmax - xmin) >= 2, as.character(first(tou_period)), ""),
    label_col = tou_colors[as.character(first(tou_period))],
    .groups   = "drop"
  )

lines_overlay_df <- hourly_overlay |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(`Baseline (No Batteries)`, `Random 5% Rollout`, `Targeted 5% Rollout (Segment 2)`),
    names_to  = "scenario",
    values_to = "total_mwh"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    scenario = factor(
      scenario,
      levels = c(
        "Baseline (No Batteries)",
        "Random 5% Rollout",
        "Targeted 5% Rollout (Segment 2)"
      )
    )
  )

scenario_colors <- c(
  "Baseline (No Batteries)"         = "#1B2A4A",
  "Random 5% Rollout"               = "#7C3AED",
  "Targeted 5% Rollout (Segment 2)" = "#D92D20"
)

scenario_linetypes <- c(
  "Baseline (No Batteries)"         = "solid",
  "Random 5% Rollout"               = "dashed",
  "Targeted 5% Rollout (Segment 2)" = "solid"
)

p_overlay_ts <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(
    data = shade_blocks,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tou_period),
    alpha = 0.16
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = shade_blocks,
    aes(x = mid_x, y = Inf, label = label, color = I(label_col)),
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  geom_line(
    data = lines_overlay_df,
    aes(
      x = hour_ending - 0.5,
      y = total_mwh,
      color = scenario,
      linetype = scenario,
      linewidth = scenario
    )
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tou_colors, name = "TOU Window") +
  scale_color_manual(values = scenario_colors, name = "Deployment Strategy") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = scenario_linetypes, name = "Deployment Strategy") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(
    values = c(
      "Baseline (No Batteries)"         = 0.95,
      "Random 5% Rollout"               = 1.05,
      "Targeted 5% Rollout (Segment 2)" = 1.25
    ),
    name = "Deployment Strategy"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
    labels = c("12am", "4am", "8am", "12pm", "4pm", "8pm", "12am"),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = comma,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.22))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Targeted Segment 2 vs. Random 5% Battery Rollout Across NYSEG TOU Periods",
    subtitle = "Equal fleet battery budget (5% of meters, Enphase IQ Battery 10C): Segment 2 targeting delivers deeper Peak shaving per unit",
    x = "Time of Day",
    y = "Total Weekday Usage (MWh)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12.5) +
  theme(
    plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    legend.position  = "top",
    legend.box       = "vertical",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing    = unit(1.1, "lines")
  )

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. COMPUTE ANNUAL CUSTOMER BILLS ACROSS ALL 3 STRATEGIES & BOTH TARIFFS
# ==============================================================================
tou_deliv <- 0.07011; tou_fixed <- 30.00
std_deliv <- 0.09138; std_fixed <- 19.00

cust_annual_bills <- sim_all |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    n_months  = n_distinct(month),
    kwh_base  = sum(kwh_baseline),
    kwh_rand  = sum(kwh_random_5pct),
    kwh_targ  = sum(kwh_targeted_5pct),

    # Annual bills if billed on Standard ($19/mo + $0.09138/kWh + standard_rate)
    bill_std_base = sum(kwh_baseline      * (standard_rate + std_deliv)) + std_fixed * n_months,
    bill_std_rand = sum(kwh_random_5pct   * (standard_rate + std_deliv)) + std_fixed * n_months,
    bill_std_targ = sum(kwh_targeted_5pct * (standard_rate + std_deliv)) + std_fixed * n_months,

    # Annual bills if billed on SC12 TOU ($30/mo + $0.07011/kWh + tou_rate)
    bill_tou_base = sum(kwh_baseline      * (tou_rate + tou_deliv)) + tou_fixed * n_months,
    bill_tou_rand = sum(kwh_random_5pct   * (tou_rate + tou_deliv)) + tou_fixed * n_months,
    bill_tou_targ = sum(kwh_targeted_5pct * (tou_rate + tou_deliv)) + tou_fixed * n_months,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    is_sc12_elig = kwh_base >= 35000,
    in_rand_5pct = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% random_5pct_custs,
    in_targ_5pct = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% targeted_seg2_5pct_custs,

    # Regime A: Current NYSEG Rules (only >=35,000 kWh/yr accounts get SC12 TOU)
    cur_base = if_else(is_sc12_elig, bill_tou_base, bill_std_base),
    cur_rand = if_else(is_sc12_elig, bill_tou_rand, bill_std_rand),
    cur_targ = if_else(is_sc12_elig, bill_tou_targ, bill_std_targ),

    # Regime B: BESS Tariff Waiver (battery adopters also qualify for SC12 TOU)
    waiv_base = if_else(is_sc12_elig, bill_tou_base, bill_std_base),
    waiv_rand = if_else(is_sc12_elig | in_rand_5pct, bill_tou_rand, bill_std_rand),
    waiv_targ = if_else(is_sc12_elig | in_targ_5pct, bill_tou_targ, bill_std_targ)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 2. FLEET-WIDE & PER-BATTERY ANNUAL SAVINGS TABLE (ALL 3 APPROACHES)
# ==============================================================================
n_bats_rand <- sum(cust_annual_bills$in_rand_5pct)
n_bats_targ <- sum(cust_annual_bills$in_targ_5pct)

annual_pricing_comparison <- bind_rows(
  # --- Regime A: Current Tariff Rules ---
  tibble(
    tariff_regime = "A. Current Rules (SC12 requires >=35k kWh/yr)",
    strategy = c("1. Baseline (No Batteries)", "2. Random 5% Rollout", "3. Targeted 5% (Segment 2)"),
    batteries = c(0, n_bats_rand, n_bats_targ),
    fleet_annual_bill = c(
      sum(cust_annual_bills$cur_base),
      sum(cust_annual_bills$cur_rand),
      sum(cust_annual_bills$cur_targ)
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(
      fleet_annual_savings     = first(fleet_annual_bill) - fleet_annual_bill,
      savings_per_battery_year = if_else(batteries > 0, fleet_annual_savings / batteries, 0)
    ),

  # --- Regime B: SC12 Waiver for Battery Adopters ---
  tibble(
    tariff_regime = "B. With BESS TOU Waiver (Adopters get SC12)",
    strategy = c("1. Baseline (No Batteries)", "2. Random 5% Rollout", "3. Targeted 5% (Segment 2)"),
    batteries = c(0, n_bats_rand, n_bats_targ),
    fleet_annual_bill = c(
      sum(cust_annual_bills$waiv_base),
      sum(cust_annual_bills$waiv_rand),
      sum(cust_annual_bills$waiv_targ)
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(
      fleet_annual_savings     = first(fleet_annual_bill) - fleet_annual_bill,
      savings_per_battery_year = if_else(batteries > 0, fleet_annual_savings / batteries, 0)
    ),

  # --- Regime C: Pure TOU Arbitrage (All Meters on TOU) ---
  tibble(
    tariff_regime = "C. Pure TOU Arbitrage (All Meters on SC12)",
    strategy = c("1. Baseline (No Batteries)", "2. Random 5% Rollout", "3. Targeted 5% (Segment 2)"),
    batteries = c(0, n_bats_rand, n_bats_targ),
    fleet_annual_bill = c(
      sum(cust_annual_bills$bill_tou_base),
      sum(cust_annual_bills$bill_tou_rand),
      sum(cust_annual_bills$bill_tou_targ)
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(
      fleet_annual_savings     = first(fleet_annual_bill) - fleet_annual_bill,
      savings_per_battery_year = if_else(batteries > 0, fleet_annual_savings / batteries, 0)
    )
)

annual_pricing_comparison

# 3. ADOPTER-ONLY BILL BREAKDOWN (WHAT AN INDIVIDUAL BATTERY HOUSEHOLD SEES)
# ==============================================================================
adopter_bill_summary <- bind_rows(

# ANNIES CODE
APPLYING THE BATTERY FOR OUR GROUPS OF INTEREST

```{r}
library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2); library(scales); library(readr)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOAD CHARACTERISTICS & DEFINE TARGETING SCENARIOS
# ==============================================================================
chars <- read_csv("customer_characteristics.csv") |>
  mutate(across(-CUSTOMER_NUMBER, ~ as.logical(.x))) |>
  filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER))

all_custs <- unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
n_target  <- round(0.015 * length(all_custs))   # same fleet size in every scenario

# Average usage per customer, used to rank "high use" customers in scenario 3
cust_use <- sub_df |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(total_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh), .groups = "drop")

# Helper: take n_target from an eligible pool (all of them if the pool is smaller)
pick <- function(ids, n = n_target) {
  if (length(ids) <= n) {
    message("Eligible pool (", length(ids), ") <= target (", n, "): using all of them")
    return(ids)
  }
  sample(ids, n)
}

set.seed(42)

# 0) Baseline comparison: random 5%
ids_random <- sample(all_custs, n_target)

# 1) Open to new/green tech: solar, heat pump, or EV
ids_green <- chars |>
  filter(is_solar | heatpump | lvl1EV | lvl2EV) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |> pick()

# 2) High peak / off-peak ratio
ids_ratio <- chars |>
  filter(high_peak_ratio) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |> pick()

# 3) High-use "typical curve": not solar, no EV, peak contributor.
#    Ranked by total usage so the heaviest users get the batteries.
ids_typical <- chars |>
  filter(peak_demand_contributor, !is_solar, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV) |>
  inner_join(cust_use, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER") |>
  slice_max(total_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

scenarios <- list(
  "Random 5%"                      = ids_random,
  "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)" = ids_green,
  "High peak/off-peak ratio"       = ids_ratio,
  "High-use, typical curve"        = ids_typical
)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. SIMULATION FUNCTION (your dispatch logic, unchanged)
# ==============================================================================
cap_kwh <- 20.16; max_kw <- 7.68; rt_eff <- 0.894
eta <- sqrt(rt_eff); taper_frac <- 0.45

simulate_battery <- function(battery_custs) {
  bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
    filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs) |>
    mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
    complete(nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
             hour_ending = 1:24, fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

  kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = avg_kw_before)
  kw_mat <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  n_prof <- nrow(kw_mat)

  per_wide <- kw_wide |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
    left_join(df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
              by = c("month", "day_type"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = tou_period)
  per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0

  soc <- rep(0, n_prof); out_mat <- kw_mat
  for (pass in 1:2) {
    for (h in 1:24) {
      l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0); p <- per_mat[, h]

      is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
      grid_charge <- ifelse(is_charge,
                            pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta), 0)
      soc <- soc + grid_charge * eta

      is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
        (soc > 0) & (l > 0)
      deliver <- ifelse(is_discharge, pmin(l, max_kw, soc * eta), 0)
      soc <- soc - deliver / eta

      if (pass == 2) out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
    }
  }

  bat_after_long <- bind_cols(kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                              as_tibble(out_mat)) |>
    pivot_longer(as.character(1:24), names_to = "hour_ending", values_to = "avg_kw_after") |>
    mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

  sub_df |>
    left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    mutate(
      has_battery = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs,
      kwh_before  = hourly_kwh,
      kwh_after   = if_else(has_battery, avg_kw_after * n_hours, hourly_kwh),
      cost_before = kwh_before * tou_rate,
      cost_after  = kwh_after  * tou_rate
    )
}

sims <- lapply(scenarios, simulate_battery)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. SCENARIO COMPARISON TABLE (fleet-level, by TOU period)
# ==============================================================================
comparison <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sims), function(nm) {
  sims[[nm]] |>
    group_by(tou_period) |>
    summarise(mwh_before = sum(kwh_before) / 1000,
              mwh_after  = sum(kwh_after)  / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(scenario = nm,
           n_batteries = length(scenarios[[nm]]),
           mwh_diff = mwh_after - mwh_before,
           pct_change = mwh_diff / mwh_before * 100)
})) |>
  arrange(factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak")), scenario)

comparison

# Also useful: who are these groups, and how much do they overlap?
sapply(scenarios, length)
table(green = all_custs %in% ids_green, ratio = all_custs %in% ids_ratio)

# ==============================================================================
# 4. PLOT FUNCTION (your plot, parameterized) + one plot per scenario
# ==============================================================================
tou_colors <- c("Off-peak" = "#0077C8", "Mid-peak" = "#00853E", "Peak" = "#B57A14")

plot_sim <- function(sim_df, scen_name) {
  hourly_season_sim <- sim_df |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday") |>
    mutate(
      season = factor(case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)",
        month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring (Mar–May)",
        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)"),
        levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Spring (Mar–May)",
                   "Summer (Jun–Aug)", "Fall (Sep–Nov)")),
      tou_period = factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak"))
    ) |>
    group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
    summarise(Before = sum(kwh_before) / 1000, After = sum(kwh_after) / 1000,
              .groups = "drop") |>
    arrange(season, hour_ending)

  shade_blocks <- hourly_season_sim |>
    group_by(season) |>
    mutate(block_id = cumsum(tou_period != lag(tou_period, default = first(tou_period)))) |>
    group_by(season, block_id, tou_period) |>
    summarise(xmin = min(hour_ending) - 1, xmax = max(hour_ending),
              mid_x = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
              label = if_else((xmax - xmin) >= 2, as.character(first(tou_period)), ""),
              .groups = "drop")

  lines_df <- hourly_season_sim |>
    pivot_longer(c(Before, After), names_to = "scenario", values_to = "total_mwh") |>
    mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = c("Before", "After"),
                             labels = c("Before Battery (Baseline)", "After Battery")))

  ggplot() +
    geom_rect(data = shade_blocks,
              aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tou_period),
              alpha = 0.18) +
    geom_text(data = shade_blocks,
              aes(x = mid_x, y = Inf, label = label, color = tou_period),
              vjust = 1.5, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_line(data = lines_df,
              aes(x = hour_ending - 0.5, y = total_mwh, linetype = scenario, linewidth = scenario),
              color = "#1B2A4A") +
    geom_point(data = lines_df,
               aes(x = hour_ending - 0.5, y = total_mwh, shape = scenario),
               color = "#1B2A4A", size = 1.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = tou_colors, name = "TOU Window") +
    scale_color_manual(values = tou_colors, guide = "none") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c("solid", "dashed"), name = "Fleet Scenario") +
    scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(1.0, 1.15), name = "Fleet Scenario") +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17), name = "Fleet Scenario") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
                       labels = c("12am", "4am", "8am", "12pm", "4pm", "8pm", "12am"),
                       expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.22))) +
    labs(title = paste0("Fleet Load Shift: ", scen_name),
         subtitle = paste0(length(scenarios[[scen_name]]),
                           " customers with Enphase IQ Battery 10C (20.16 kWh, 7.68 kW, 89.4% RTE)"),
         x = "Time of Day", y = "Total Weekday Usage (MWh)") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical",
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.spacing = unit(1.1, "lines"))
}

plots <- lapply(names(sims), function(nm) plot_sim(sims[[nm]], nm))
names(plots) <- names(sims)
plots[["Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"]]
plots[["High peak/off-peak ratio"]]
plots[["High-use, typical curve"]]

# ==============================================================================
# SINGLE PLOT: 4 seasons, each with Baseline + 3 targeting-group lines
# ==============================================================================
group_names <- c("Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                 "High-use, typical curve")

add_season <- function(df) {
  df |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday") |>
    mutate(
      season = factor(case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)",

    )
}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

# Helper to assign seasons consistently with your plots
assign_season <- function(m) {
  factor(case_when(
    m %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)",
    m %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring (Mar–May)",
    m %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
    TRUE               ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)"
  ), levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Spring (Mar–May)", 
                "Summer (Jun–Aug)", "Fall (Sep–Nov)"))
}

# ==============================================================================
# 1. FLEET CAPACITY & ANNUAL CUSTOMER SAVINGS (PER BATTERY HOUSEHOLD)
# ==============================================================================
fleet_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sims), function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]]
  n_bat  <- length(scenarios[[nm]])
  
  # Check hours represented per customer to ensure exact annualization (8,760 hrs/yr)
  hrs_per_cust <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(tot_hrs = sum(n_hours), .groups = "drop") |>
    summarise(mean_hrs = mean(tot_hrs)) |>
    pull(mean_hrs)
  
  ann_factor <- 8760 / hrs_per_cust
  
  # Bill impact restricted to the ~5,000 customers who actually received a battery
  bat_savings <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(
      bill_before = sum(cost_before) * ann_factor,
      bill_after  = sum(cost_after)  * ann_factor,
      savings     = bill_before - bill_after,
      .groups     = "drop"
    )
  
  tibble(
    scenario             = nm,
    n_batteries          = n_bat,
    fleet_energy_mwh     = (n_bat * cap_kwh) / 1000,
    fleet_power_mw       = (n_bat * max_kw)  / 1000,
    avg_bill_before      = mean(bat_savings$bill_before),
    avg_bill_after       = mean(bat_savings$bill_after),
    mean_annual_savings  = mean(bat_savings$savings),
    median_annual_saving = median(bat_savings$savings),
    total_fleet_savings  = sum(bat_savings$savings)
  )
}))

print(fleet_summary)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. SEASONAL PEAK RELIEF (MATCHING YOUR WEEKDAY PLOT & DISPATCH LOGIC)
# ==============================================================================
seasonal_peak_relief <- bind_rows(lapply(names(sims), function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]] |>
    mutate(season = assign_season(month))
  
  # Identify which season-day_types actually have a "Peak" TOU window
  # (Matches your dispatch rule: discharge in Peak if available, else Mid-peak)
  discharge_windows <- df_sim |>
    group_by(season, day_type) |>
    summarise(has_peak = any(tou_period == "Peak"), .groups = "drop")
  
  df_sim |>
    left_join(discharge_windows, by = c("season", "day_type")) |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday") |>
    # Filter to the active discharge window (Peak, or Mid-peak if no Peak exists)
    filter((has_peak & tou_period == "Peak") | (!has_peak & tou_period == "Mid-peak")) |>
    group_by(season, tou_period) |>
    summarise(
      # Total weekday MWh shaved across the season (the area between lines in your plot)
      mwh_before        = sum(kwh_before) / 1000,
      mwh_after         = sum(kwh_after)  / 1000,
      mwh_relief        = mwh_before - mwh_after,
      pct_peak_shaved   = (mwh_relief / mwh_before) * 100,
      # Average hourly MW reduction during the weekday discharge window
      avg_mw_relief     = sum(kwh_before - kwh_after) / sum(n_hours / n_distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) / 1000,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(scenario = nm)
})) |>
  select(scenario, season, discharge_tou = tou_period, 
         mwh_before, mwh_after, mwh_relief, pct_peak_shaved, avg_mw_relief) |>
  arrange(season, desc(mwh_relief))

print(seasonal_peak_relief, n = 20)

# Wide side-by-side comparison table of Seasonal Peak Relief (MWh shaved)
seasonal_relief_wide <- seasonal_peak_relief |>
  select(scenario, season, mwh_relief) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = season, values_from = mwh_relief) |>
  mutate(Total_Annual_Weekday_Relief_MWh = rowSums(across(-scenario)))

print(seasonal_relief_wide)

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOAD CHARACTERISTICS & DEFINE TARGETING SCENARIOS (WITH 5TH GROUP)
# ==============================================================================
chars <- read_csv("customer_characteristics.csv") |>
  mutate(across(-CUSTOMER_NUMBER, ~ as.logical(.x))) |>
  filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER))

all_custs <- unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
n_target  <- round(0.015 * length(all_custs))   # 1.5% launch target

# Total usage (for Scenario 3) and Peak-window usage (for Scenario 4 / Group 5)
cust_use <- sub_df |>
  group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
  summarise(
    total_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh),
    peak_kwh  = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pick <- function(ids, n = n_target) {
  if (length(ids) <= n) {
    message("Eligible pool (", length(ids), ") <= target (", n, "): using all of them")
    return(ids)
  }
  sample(ids, n)
}

set.seed(42)

# 0) Baseline comparison: random 1.5%
ids_random <- sample(all_custs, n_target)

# 1) Open to new/green tech: solar, heat pump, or EV
ids_green <- chars |>
  filter(is_solar | heatpump | lvl1EV | lvl2EV) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |> pick()

# 2) High peak / off-peak ratio
ids_ratio <- chars |>
  filter(high_peak_ratio) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |> pick()

# 3) High-use "typical curve": not solar, no EV, peak contributor (ranked by total kWh)
ids_typical <- chars |>
  filter(peak_demand_contributor, !is_solar, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV) |>
  inner_join(cust_use, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER") |>
  slice_max(total_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

# 4) NEW 5TH GROUP — Inflexible (no HP, no EV, no solar) with high peak usage
ids_inflexible <- chars |>
  filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
  inner_join(cust_use, by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER") |>
  slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

scenarios <- list(
  "Random 1.5%"                                    = ids_random,
  "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"              = ids_green,
  "High peak/off-peak ratio"                       = ids_ratio,
  "High-use, typical curve"                        = ids_typical,
  "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"   = ids_inflexible
)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. SIMULATION FUNCTION (your dispatch logic, unchanged)
# ==============================================================================
cap_kwh <- 20.16; max_kw <- 7.68; rt_eff <- 0.894
eta <- sqrt(rt_eff); taper_frac <- 0.45

simulate_battery <- function(battery_custs) {
  bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
    filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs) |>
    mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
    complete(nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
             hour_ending = 1:24, fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

  kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = avg_kw_before)
  kw_mat <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  n_prof <- nrow(kw_mat)

  per_wide <- kw_wide |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
    left_join(df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
              by = c("month", "day_type"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = tou_period)
  per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0

  soc <- rep(0, n_prof); out_mat <- kw_mat
  for (pass in 1:2) {
    for (h in 1:24) {
      l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0); p <- per_mat[, h]

      is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
      grid_charge <- ifelse(is_charge,
                            pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta), 0)
      soc <- soc + grid_charge * eta

      is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
        (soc > 0) & (l > 0)
      deliver <- ifelse(is_discharge, pmin(l, max_kw, soc * eta), 0)
      soc <- soc - deliver / eta

      if (pass == 2) out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
    }
  }

  bat_after_long <- bind_cols(kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                              as_tibble(out_mat)) |>
    pivot_longer(as.character(1:24), names_to = "hour_ending", values_to = "avg_kw_after") |>
    mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

  sub_df |>
    left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    mutate(
      has_battery = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs,
      kwh_before  = hourly_kwh,
      kwh_after   = if_else(has_battery, avg_kw_after * n_hours, hourly_kwh),
      cost_before = kwh_before * tou_rate,
      cost_after  = kwh_after  * tou_rate
    )
}

sims <- lapply(scenarios, simulate_battery)

# ==============================================================================

           n_batteries = length(scenarios[[nm]]),
           mwh_diff = mwh_after - mwh_before,
           pct_change = mwh_diff / mwh_before * 100)
})) |>
  arrange(factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak")), scenario)

        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)"),
        levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Spring (Mar–May)",
                   "Summer (Jun–Aug)", "Fall (Sep–Nov)")),
      tou_period = factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak"))
    )
}

# Baseline (identical across scenarios, so take it from the first sim)
baseline_df <- add_season(sims[[group_names[1]]]) |>
  group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
  summarise(total_mwh = sum(kwh_before) / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(scenario = "Baseline (no batteries)")

# One "after battery" line per targeting group
after_df <- bind_rows(lapply(group_names, function(nm) {
  add_season(sims[[nm]]) |>
    group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
    summarise(total_mwh = sum(kwh_after) / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(scenario = nm)
}))

scen_levels <- c("Baseline (no batteries)", group_names)
lines_df <- bind_rows(baseline_df, after_df) |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scen_levels)) |>
  arrange(scenario, season, hour_ending)

# Shaded TOU background blocks & labels
shade_blocks <- baseline_df |>
  group_by(season) |>
  mutate(block_id = cumsum(tou_period != lag(tou_period, default = first(tou_period)))) |>
  group_by(season, block_id, tou_period) |>
  summarise(xmin = min(hour_ending) - 1, xmax = max(hour_ending),
            mid_x = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
            label = if_else((xmax - xmin) >= 2, as.character(first(tou_period)), ""),
            .groups = "drop")

tou_colors <- c("Off-peak" = "#0077C8", "Mid-peak" = "#00853E", "Peak" = "#B57A14")

line_colors <- c("Baseline (no batteries)"                       = "#1B2A4A",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

line_types <- c("solid", "dashed", "dotdash", "twodash")
names(line_types) <- scen_levels

p_all <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = shade_blocks,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tou_period),
            alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_text(data = shade_blocks,
            aes(x = mid_x, y = Inf, label = label),
            color = "grey30", vjust = 1.5, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_line(data = lines_df,
            aes(x = hour_ending - 0.5, y = total_mwh,
                color = scenario, linetype = scenario, linewidth = scenario)) +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tou_colors, name = "TOU Window") +
  scale_color_manual(values = line_colors, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = line_types, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(1.2, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9) |> setNames(scen_levels),
                         name = "Scenario") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
                     labels = c("12am", "4am", "8am", "12pm", "4pm", "8pm", "12am"),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.22))) +
  labs(title = "Fleet Load Shift by Battery Targeting Strategy",
       subtitle = paste0("Enphase IQ Battery 10C (20.16 kWh, 7.68 kW, 89.4% RTE) on ",
                         length(scenarios[[group_names[1]]]),
                         " customers per scenario (1.5% of fleet)"),
       x = "Time of Day", y = "Total Weekday Usage (MWh)") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
         linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
         linewidth = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.1, "lines"))

library(dplyr)

# ==============================================================================
inflex_name <- "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"
if (!inflex_name %in% names(sims)) {
  ids_inflexible <- chars |>
    filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
    inner_join(
      sub_df |>
        group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
        summarise(peak_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
    ) |>
    slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

  scenarios[[inflex_name]] <- ids_inflexible
  sims[[inflex_name]]      <- simulate_battery(ids_inflexible)
}

# Two-step scaling: 5,000 sample -> 35,000 full dataset -> 924,544 NYSEG territory
n_sub_custs        <- length(unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) # 5,000
n_dataset_custs    <- 35000                                   # Full dataset
n_nyseg_custs      <- 924544                                  # NYSEG territory

scale_sub_to_35k   <- n_dataset_custs / n_sub_custs           # 7.0x
scale_35k_to_nyseg <- n_nyseg_custs / n_dataset_custs         # 26.4155x
scale_sub_to_nyseg <- scale_sub_to_35k * scale_35k_to_nyseg   # 184.9088x

scen_order <- c("Random 1.5%",
                "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)")
scen_order <- intersect(scen_order, names(sims))

scen_colors <- c("Random 1.5%"                                   = "#7F7F7F",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

# Scaled fleet capacity across all three tiers (1.5% adoption)
n_bat_sub   <- length(scenarios[[scen_order[1]]])       # 75
n_bat_35k   <- round(n_bat_sub * scale_sub_to_35k)      # 525
n_bat_nyseg <- round(n_bat_sub * scale_sub_to_nyseg)    # 13,868

cap_sub_label <- sprintf(
  "Added Capacity (1.5%%): 5k Sample = %s bats (%.2f MWh / %.2f MW)  |  35k Dataset = %s bats (%.1f MWh / %.1f MW)  |  NYSEG = %s bats (%.1f MWh / %.1f MW)",
  comma(n_bat_sub),   (n_bat_sub   * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_sub   * max_kw) / 1000,
  comma(n_bat_35k),   (n_bat_35k   * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_35k   * max_kw) / 1000,
  comma(n_bat_nyseg), (n_bat_nyseg * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_nyseg * max_kw) / 1000
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. COMPUTE METRICS WITH TWO-STEP SCALING
# ==============================================================================
savings_df <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]]

  hrs_per_cust <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(tot_hrs = sum(n_hours), .groups = "drop") |>
    summarise(mean_hrs = mean(tot_hrs)) |>
    pull(mean_hrs)
  ann_factor <- 8760 / hrs_per_cust

  cust_savings <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(annual_saved = (sum(cost_before) - sum(cost_after)) * ann_factor,
              .groups = "drop")

  sub_total_saved <- sum(cust_savings$annual_saved)

  tibble(
    scenario          = factor(nm, levels = rev(scen_order)),
    per_cust_usd      = mean(cust_savings$annual_saved),
    dataset_35k_k     = (sub_total_saved * scale_sub_to_35k)   / 1e3,
    nyseg_total_m     = (sub_total_saved * scale_sub_to_nyseg) / 1e6
  )
}))

peak_df <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]] |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday", month %in% c(12, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8)) |>
    mutate(season = factor(if_else(month %in% c(12, 1, 2), "Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)"),
                           levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)")))

  season_window <- df_sim |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(target_tou = if_else(any(tou_period == "Peak"), "Peak", "Mid-peak"),
              .groups = "drop")

  df_sim |>
    inner_join(season_window, by = c("season", "tou_period" = "target_tou")) |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(
      n_peak_days            = sum(n_hours) / (n_distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) * n_distinct(hour_ending)),
      # Percentage drops are scale-invariant (identical across 5k, 35k, and 924.5k)
      fleet_peak_pct_drop    = (1 - sum(kwh_after) / sum(kwh_before)) * 100,
      enrolled_peak_pct_drop = (1 - sum(kwh_after[has_battery]) / sum(kwh_before[has_battery])) * 100,
      # Single peak event MWh scaled from 5k -> 35k -> NYSEG
      sub_single_mwh         = ((sum(kwh_before) - sum(kwh_after)) / 1000) / n_peak_days,
      dataset_35k_single_mwh = sub_single_mwh * scale_sub_to_35k,
      nyseg_single_mwh       = sub_single_mwh * scale_sub_to_nyseg,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(scenario = factor(nm, levels = rev(scen_order)))
}))

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 1: WINTER & SUMMER PEAK LOAD REDUCTION (% DROP — SCALE-INVARIANT)
# ==============================================================================
plot1_data <- peak_df |>

         `Enrolled Cohort Peak Drop (%)`    = enrolled_peak_pct_drop,

p_peak_pct <- ggplot(plot1_data, aes(x = pct_drop, y = scenario, fill = season)) +

  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),

       subtitle = cap_sub_label,
       x = "Peak-Window Usage Reduction (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_peak_pct

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 2: SINGLE PEAK EVENT MWh SAVED (35k DATASET VS. NYSEG SCALE)
# ==============================================================================
plot2_data <- peak_df |>
  select(scenario, season,
         `Full Dataset (35,000 Customers)`     = dataset_35k_single_mwh,

p_single_peak <- ggplot(plot2_data, aes(x = mwh_saved, y = scenario, fill = season)) +

                               "Summer (Jun–Aug)" = "#E67E22"),
                    name = "Season") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(title = "Energy Shaved During a Single Weekday Peak Event",
       subtitle = cap_sub_label,
       x = "Single Peak Event Reduction (MWh)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_single_peak

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 3: ANNUAL TOU COST SAVINGS (PER CUSTOMER, 35k DATASET, & NYSEG SCALE)
# ==============================================================================
plot3_data <- savings_df |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(per_cust_usd, dataset_35k_k, nyseg_total_m),

```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. REALISTIC BATTERY SIMULATION (WITH 20% BACKUP RESERVE FLOOR)
# ==============================================================================
cap_kwh      <- 20.16
max_kw       <- 7.68
rt_eff       <- 0.894
eta          <- sqrt(rt_eff)
taper_frac   <- 0.45
min_soc_frac <- 0.20                    # Never drain below 20% (outage backup reserve)
min_soc_kwh  <- cap_kwh * min_soc_frac  # 4.032 kWh reserve floor (16.13 kWh usable)

simulate_battery <- function(battery_custs) {
  bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
    filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs) |>
    mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
    complete(nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
             hour_ending = 1:24, fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

  kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = avg_kw_before)
  kw_mat <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  n_prof <- nrow(kw_mat)

  per_wide <- kw_wide |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
    left_join(df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
              by = c("month", "day_type"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = tou_period)
  per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0

  # Initialize SOC at the 20% backup reserve floor rather than 0
  soc <- rep(min_soc_kwh, n_prof)
  out_mat <- kw_mat

  for (pass in 1:2) {
    for (h in 1:24) {
      l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0)
      p <- per_mat[, h]

      is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
      grid_charge <- ifelse(is_charge,
                            pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta), 0)
      soc <- soc + grid_charge * eta

      # Only discharge energy above the 20% reserve floor (soc > min_soc_kwh)
      is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
        (soc > min_soc_kwh) & (l > 0)
      deliver <- ifelse(is_discharge, pmin(l, max_kw, (soc - min_soc_kwh) * eta), 0)
      soc <- soc - deliver / eta

      if (pass == 2) out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
    }
  }

  bat_after_long <- bind_cols(kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                              as_tibble(out_mat)) |>
    pivot_longer(as.character(1:24), names_to = "hour_ending", values_to = "avg_kw_after") |>
    mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

  sub_df |>
    left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    mutate(
      has_battery = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs,
      kwh_before  = hourly_kwh,
      kwh_after   = if_else(has_battery, avg_kw_after * n_hours, hourly_kwh),
      cost_before = kwh_before * tou_rate,
      cost_after  = kwh_after  * tou_rate
    )
}

# Ensure all 4 active scenarios are defined and re-simulated with the 20% reserve floor
names(scenarios)[names(scenarios) == "Random 5%"] <- "Random 1.5%"
inflex_name <- "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"

if (!inflex_name %in% names(scenarios)) {
  scenarios[[inflex_name]] <- chars |>
    filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
    inner_join(
      sub_df |>
        group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
        summarise(peak_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
    ) |>
    slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
}

scen_order <- c("Random 1.5%",
                "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)")

scen_colors <- c("Random 1.5%"                                   = "#7F7F7F",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

# Re-run simulations with the 20% SOC floor
sims <- lapply(scenarios[scen_order], simulate_battery)

# Two-step scaling: 5,000 sample -> 35,000 dataset -> 924,544 NYSEG territory
n_sub_custs        <- length(unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) # 5,000
scale_sub_to_35k   <- 35000 / n_sub_custs                     # 7.0x
scale_sub_to_nyseg <- 924544 / n_sub_custs                    # 184.91x

# ==============================================================================
# 2. IDENTIFY THE TOP 100 CRITICAL GRID HOURS OF THE YEAR ("TOP 1%" RULE)
# ==============================================================================
# Rank all (month, day_type, hour_ending) buckets by baseline fleet hourly demand
# and select the exact 100 highest-load hours of the 8,760-hour year.
top100_slots <- sub_df |>
  group_by(month, day_type, hour_ending) |>
  summarise(
    slot_hours    = round(median(n_hours[n_hours > 0], na.rm = TRUE)),
    sub_mw_before = sum(if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) / 1000,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(sub_mw_before)) |>
  mutate(
    cum_hours    = cumsum(slot_hours),
    prev_hours   = lag(cum_hours, default = 0),
    weight_hours = pmax(0L, as.integer(pmin(slot_hours, 100L - prev_hours)))
  ) |>
  filter(weight_hours > 0)

# Evaluate each segment across those Top 100 Critical Hours
top100_hourly <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  sims[[nm]] |>
    inner_join(top100_slots |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, weight_hours),
               by = c("month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    group_by(month, day_type, hour_ending, weight_hours) |>
    summarise(
      sub_mw_before      = sum(if_else(n_hours > 0, kwh_before / n_hours, 0)) / 1000,
      sub_mw_after       = sum(if_else(n_hours > 0, kwh_after  / n_hours, 0)) / 1000,
      sub_mwh_saved_hr   = sub_mw_before - sub_mw_after,
      ds35k_mwh_saved_hr = sub_mwh_saved_hr * scale_sub_to_35k,
      nyseg_mwh_saved_hr = sub_mwh_saved_hr * scale_sub_to_nyseg,
      fleet_pct_drop     = (sub_mwh_saved_hr / sub_mw_before) * 100,
      enrolled_pct_drop  = (1 - sum(kwh_after[has_battery]) / sum(kwh_before[has_battery])) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange(desc(sub_mw_before)) |>
    # Expand each calendar bucket into individual ranked hours (1 to 100)
    tidyr::uncount(weight_hours) |>
    mutate(
      critical_hour_rank = row_number(),
      scenario = factor(nm, levels = scen_order)
    )
}))

# Summary Table across the Top 100 Hours
top100_summary <- top100_hourly |>
  group_by(scenario) |>
  summarise(
    avg_hourly_mwh_35k     = mean(ds35k_mwh_saved_hr),
    avg_hourly_mwh_nyseg   = mean(nyseg_mwh_saved_hr),
    total_100hr_mwh_nyseg  = sum(nyseg_mwh_saved_hr),
    avg_fleet_pct_drop     = mean(fleet_pct_drop),

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. ENSURE 20% BACKUP RESERVE SIMULATION IS APPLIED TO ALL TARGET GROUPS
# ==============================================================================
cap_kwh      <- 20.16
max_kw       <- 7.68
rt_eff       <- 0.894
eta          <- sqrt(rt_eff)
taper_frac   <- 0.45
min_soc_frac <- 0.20                    # 20% outage backup reserve floor
min_soc_kwh  <- cap_kwh * min_soc_frac  # 4.032 kWh floor (16.13 kWh usable)

simulate_battery <- function(battery_custs) {
  bat_profiles <- sub_df |>
    filter(CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs) |>
    mutate(avg_kw_before = if_else(n_hours > 0, hourly_kwh / n_hours, 0)) |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending, avg_kw_before) |>
    complete(nesting(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
             hour_ending = 1:24, fill = list(avg_kw_before = 0)) |>
    arrange(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type, hour_ending)

  kw_wide <- bat_profiles |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = avg_kw_before)
  kw_mat <- as.matrix(kw_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  n_prof <- nrow(kw_mat)

  per_wide <- kw_wide |>
    select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type) |>
    left_join(df |> select(month, day_type, hour_ending, tou_period),
              by = c("month", "day_type"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                names_from = hour_ending, values_from = tou_period)
  per_mat <- as.matrix(per_wide[, as.character(1:24)])
  has_peak_day <- rowSums(per_mat == "Peak") > 0

  soc <- rep(min_soc_kwh, n_prof)
  out_mat <- kw_mat

  for (pass in 1:2) {
    for (h in 1:24) {
      l <- pmax(kw_mat[, h], 0)
      p <- per_mat[, h]

      is_charge   <- (p == "Off-peak") & (soc < cap_kwh)
      grid_charge <- ifelse(is_charge,
                            pmin(max_kw, ((cap_kwh - soc) * taper_frac) / eta), 0)
      soc <- soc + grid_charge * eta

      is_discharge <- ((has_peak_day & p == "Peak") | (!has_peak_day & p == "Mid-peak")) &
        (soc > min_soc_kwh) & (l > 0)
      deliver <- ifelse(is_discharge, pmin(l, max_kw, (soc - min_soc_kwh) * eta), 0)
      soc <- soc - deliver / eta

      if (pass == 2) out_mat[, h] <- kw_mat[, h] + grid_charge - deliver
    }
  }

  bat_after_long <- bind_cols(kw_wide |> select(CUSTOMER_NUMBER, month, day_type),
                              as_tibble(out_mat)) |>
    pivot_longer(as.character(1:24), names_to = "hour_ending", values_to = "avg_kw_after") |>
    mutate(hour_ending = as.integer(hour_ending))

  sub_df |>
    left_join(bat_after_long, by = c("CUSTOMER_NUMBER", "month", "day_type", "hour_ending")) |>
    mutate(
      has_battery = CUSTOMER_NUMBER %in% battery_custs,
      kwh_before  = hourly_kwh,
      kwh_after   = if_else(has_battery, avg_kw_after * n_hours, hourly_kwh),
      cost_before = kwh_before * tou_rate,
      cost_after  = kwh_after  * tou_rate
    )
}

inflex_name <- "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"
if (!inflex_name %in% names(scenarios)) {
  scenarios[[inflex_name]] <- chars |>
    filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
    inner_join(
      sub_df |>
        group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
        summarise(peak_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
    ) |>
    slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)
}

group_names <- c("Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)")

# Re-run simulations for the 3 plotted groups with the 20% reserve floor
sims_20pct <- lapply(scenarios[group_names], simulate_battery)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. SINGLE OVERLAY PLOT: 4 SEASONS, BASELINE + 3 TARGETING GROUPS (20% RESERVE)
# ==============================================================================
add_season <- function(df) {
  df |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday") |>
    mutate(
      season = factor(case_when(
        month %in% c(12, 1, 2) ~ "Winter (Dec–Feb)",
        month %in% c(3, 4, 5)  ~ "Spring (Mar–May)",
        month %in% c(6, 7, 8)  ~ "Summer (Jun–Aug)",
        TRUE                   ~ "Fall (Sep–Nov)"),
        levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Spring (Mar–May)",
                   "Summer (Jun–Aug)", "Fall (Sep–Nov)")),
      tou_period = factor(tou_period, levels = c("Off-peak", "Mid-peak", "Peak"))
    )
}

baseline_df <- add_season(sims_20pct[[group_names[1]]]) |>
  group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
  summarise(total_mwh = sum(kwh_before) / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(scenario = "Baseline (no batteries)")

after_df <- bind_rows(lapply(group_names, function(nm) {
  add_season(sims_20pct[[nm]]) |>
    group_by(season, hour_ending, tou_period) |>
    summarise(total_mwh = sum(kwh_after) / 1000, .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(scenario = nm)
}))

scen_levels <- c("Baseline (no batteries)", group_names)
lines_df <- bind_rows(baseline_df, after_df) |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, levels = scen_levels)) |>
  arrange(scenario, season, hour_ending)

shade_blocks <- baseline_df |>
  group_by(season) |>
  mutate(block_id = cumsum(tou_period != lag(tou_period, default = first(tou_period)))) |>
  group_by(season, block_id, tou_period) |>
  summarise(xmin = min(hour_ending) - 1, xmax = max(hour_ending),
            mid_x = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
            label = if_else((xmax - xmin) >= 2, as.character(first(tou_period)), ""),
            .groups = "drop")

tou_colors <- c("Off-peak" = "#0077C8", "Mid-peak" = "#00853E", "Peak" = "#B57A14")

line_colors <- c("Baseline (no batteries)"                       = "#1B2A4A",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

line_types <- c("solid", "dashed", "dotdash", "twodash")
names(line_types) <- scen_levels

p_all <- ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = shade_blocks,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = tou_period),
            alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_text(data = shade_blocks,
            aes(x = mid_x, y = Inf, label = label),
            color = "grey30", vjust = 1.5, size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_line(data = lines_df,
            aes(x = hour_ending - 0.5, y = total_mwh,
                color = scenario, linetype = scenario, linewidth = scenario)) +
  facet_wrap(~ season, ncol = 2, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tou_colors, name = "TOU Window") +
  scale_color_manual(values = line_colors, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = line_types, name = "Scenario") +
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c(1.2, 0.9, 0.9, 0.9) |> setNames(scen_levels),
                         name = "Scenario") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
                     labels = c("12am", "4am", "8am", "12pm", "4pm", "8pm", "12am"),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.06, 0.22))) +
  labs(title = "Fleet Load Shift by Battery Targeting Strategy",
       subtitle = paste0("Enphase IQ Battery 10C (20.16 kWh, 7.68 kW, 89.4% RTE, 20% backup reserve) on ",
                         length(scenarios[[group_names[1]]]),
                         " customers per scenario (1.5% of fleet)"),
       x = "Time of Day", y = "Total Weekday Usage (MWh)") +
  guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
         linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
         linewidth = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical",
        legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing = unit(1.1, "lines"))

p_all

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ==============================================================================
# 0. ENSURE ALL 4 SCENARIOS ARE SIMULATED & DEFINE TWO-STEP SCALING
# ==============================================================================
inflex_name <- "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"
if (!inflex_name %in% names(sims)) {
  ids_inflexible <- chars |>
    filter(!heatpump, !lvl1EV, !lvl2EV, !is_solar) |>
    inner_join(
      sub_df |>
        group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
        summarise(peak_kwh = sum(hourly_kwh[tou_period == "Peak"], na.rm = TRUE),
                  .groups = "drop"),
      by = "CUSTOMER_NUMBER"
    ) |>
    slice_max(peak_kwh, n = n_target, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    pull(CUSTOMER_NUMBER)

  scenarios[[inflex_name]] <- ids_inflexible
  sims[[inflex_name]]      <- simulate_battery(ids_inflexible)
}

# Two-step scaling: 5,000 sample -> 35,000 full dataset -> 924,544 NYSEG territory
n_sub_custs        <- length(unique(sub_df$CUSTOMER_NUMBER)) # 5,000
n_dataset_custs    <- 35000                                   # Full dataset
n_nyseg_custs      <- 924544                                  # NYSEG territory

scale_sub_to_35k   <- n_dataset_custs / n_sub_custs           # 7.0x
scale_35k_to_nyseg <- n_nyseg_custs / n_dataset_custs         # 26.4155x
scale_sub_to_nyseg <- scale_sub_to_35k * scale_35k_to_nyseg   # 184.9088x

scen_order <- c("Random 1.5%",
                "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)",
                "High peak/off-peak ratio",
                "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)")
scen_order <- intersect(scen_order, names(sims))

scen_colors <- c("Random 1.5%"                                   = "#7F7F7F",
                 "Green-tech adopters (Solar/HP/EV)"             = "#2CA02C",
                 "High peak/off-peak ratio"                      = "#D62728",
                 "Inflexible, high peak usage (No Solar/HP/EV)"  = "#9467BD")

# Scaled fleet capacity across all three tiers (1.5% adoption)
n_bat_sub   <- length(scenarios[[scen_order[1]]])       # 75
n_bat_35k   <- round(n_bat_sub * scale_sub_to_35k)      # 525
n_bat_nyseg <- round(n_bat_sub * scale_sub_to_nyseg)    # 13,868

cap_sub_label <- sprintf(
  "Added Capacity (1.5%%): 5k Sample = %s bats (%.2f MWh / %.2f MW)  |  35k Dataset = %s bats (%.1f MWh / %.1f MW)  |  NYSEG = %s bats (%.1f MWh / %.1f MW)",
  comma(n_bat_sub),   (n_bat_sub   * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_sub   * max_kw) / 1000,
  comma(n_bat_35k),   (n_bat_35k   * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_35k   * max_kw) / 1000,
  comma(n_bat_nyseg), (n_bat_nyseg * cap_kwh) / 1000, (n_bat_nyseg * max_kw) / 1000
)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. COMPUTE METRICS WITH TWO-STEP SCALING
# ==============================================================================
savings_df <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]]

  hrs_per_cust <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(tot_hrs = sum(n_hours), .groups = "drop") |>
    summarise(mean_hrs = mean(tot_hrs)) |>
    pull(mean_hrs)
  ann_factor <- 8760 / hrs_per_cust

  cust_savings <- df_sim |>
    filter(has_battery) |>
    group_by(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) |>
    summarise(annual_saved = (sum(cost_before) - sum(cost_after)) * ann_factor,
              .groups = "drop")

  sub_total_saved <- sum(cust_savings$annual_saved)

  tibble(
    scenario          = factor(nm, levels = rev(scen_order)),
    per_cust_usd      = mean(cust_savings$annual_saved),
    dataset_35k_k     = (sub_total_saved * scale_sub_to_35k)   / 1e3,
    nyseg_total_m     = (sub_total_saved * scale_sub_to_nyseg) / 1e6
  )
}))

peak_df <- bind_rows(lapply(scen_order, function(nm) {
  df_sim <- sims[[nm]] |>
    filter(day_type == "Weekday", month %in% c(12, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8)) |>
    mutate(season = factor(if_else(month %in% c(12, 1, 2), "Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)"),
                           levels = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)", "Summer (Jun–Aug)")))

  season_window <- df_sim |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(target_tou = if_else(any(tou_period == "Peak"), "Peak", "Mid-peak"),
              .groups = "drop")

  df_sim |>
    inner_join(season_window, by = c("season", "tou_period" = "target_tou")) |>
    group_by(season) |>
    summarise(
      n_peak_days            = sum(n_hours) / (n_distinct(CUSTOMER_NUMBER) * n_distinct(hour_ending)),
      # Percentage drops are scale-invariant (identical across 5k, 35k, and 924.5k)
      fleet_peak_pct_drop    = (1 - sum(kwh_after) / sum(kwh_before)) * 100,
      enrolled_peak_pct_drop = (1 - sum(kwh_after[has_battery]) / sum(kwh_before[has_battery])) * 100,
      # Single peak event MWh scaled from 5k -> 35k -> NYSEG
      sub_single_mwh         = ((sum(kwh_before) - sum(kwh_after)) / 1000) / n_peak_days,
      dataset_35k_single_mwh = sub_single_mwh * scale_sub_to_35k,
      nyseg_single_mwh       = sub_single_mwh * scale_sub_to_nyseg,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(scenario = factor(nm, levels = rev(scen_order)))
}))

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 1: WINTER & SUMMER PEAK LOAD REDUCTION (% DROP — SCALE-INVARIANT)
# ==============================================================================
plot1_data <- peak_df |>
  select(scenario, season,
         `Enrolled Cohort Peak Drop (%)`    = enrolled_peak_pct_drop,
         `Total Grid / Fleet Peak Drop (%)` = fleet_peak_pct_drop) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(`Enrolled Cohort Peak Drop (%)`, `Total Grid / Fleet Peak Drop (%)`),
               names_to = "metric", values_to = "pct_drop")

p_peak_pct <- ggplot(plot1_data, aes(x = pct_drop, y = scenario, fill = season)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.72), width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", pct_drop)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.72),
            hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold", color = "#1B2A4A") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)" = "#2B5C8F",
                               "Summer (Jun–Aug)" = "#E67E22"),
                    name = "Season") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.22))) +
  labs(title = "Predicted Peak-Window Load Reduction: Winter vs. Summer",
       subtitle = cap_sub_label,
       x = "Peak-Window Usage Reduction (%)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "grey30"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11.5),
        legend.position = "top",
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

p_peak_pct

# ==============================================================================
# PLOT 2: SINGLE PEAK EVENT MWh SAVED (35k DATASET VS. NYSEG SCALE)
# ==============================================================================
plot2_data <- peak_df |>
  select(scenario, season,
         `Full Dataset (35,000 Customers)`     = dataset_35k_single_mwh,
         `NYSEG Territory (924,544 Customers)` = nyseg_single_mwh) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(`Full Dataset (35,000 Customers)`,
                        `NYSEG Territory (924,544 Customers)`),
               names_to = "scale_tier", values_to = "mwh_saved") |>
  mutate(scale_tier = factor(scale_tier,
                             levels = c("Full Dataset (35,000 Customers)",
                                        "NYSEG Territory (924,544 Customers)")))

p_single_peak <- ggplot(plot2_data, aes(x = mwh_saved, y = scenario, fill = season)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.72), width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f MWh", mwh_saved)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.72),
            hjust = -0.12, size = 3.4, fontface = "bold", color = "#1B2A4A") +
  facet_wrap(~ scale_tier, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Winter (Dec–Feb)" = "#2B5C8F",
                               "Summer (Jun–Aug)" = "#E67E22"),
                    name = "Season") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.25))) +
  labs(title = "Energy Shaved During a Single Weekday Peak Event",
       subtitle = cap_sub_label,
       x = "Single Peak Event Reduction (MWh)", y = NULL) +
